description: Job Type: Project-based / paid test first Project Overview: I am looking for a Voice AI developer to build a **standalone Phase 1 intake-only voice agent** for a mobile mechanic / field service business. This is separate from my n8n / FieldPulse / CallTrackingMetrics automation build. Another developer is currently handling the first n8n automation proof test. For this role, I want to start with a small paid Voice AI test that proves the agent can answer calls, collect basic service request information, classify the call, and produce structured output that can later connect to n8n, CTM, and FieldPulse. Preferred platforms: **Retell AI or Vapi**. I am open to either, but I want the developer to explain which platform is better for this Phase 1 intake-only use case. ## Important Scope Boundary This first Voice AI agent is **intake only**. The agent must not: * diagnose mechanical problems, * estimate repair cost, * quote prices, * schedule appointments, * dispatch technicians, * assign technicians, * promise arrival times, * promise same-day service, * create live FieldPulse jobs, * make commitments on behalf of the business. The agent’s job is to collect information and route the call for human review/follow-up. ## What the Agent Should Do The Voice AI agent should: * Answer incoming calls professionally. * Explain that it will collect information so someone can follow up. * Collect required intake details. * Classify the call type. * Flag incomplete calls for human review. * Produce a transcript, summary, classification, missing fields, and structured JSON output. * Send or simulate an email recap and SMS alert during the test. * Be designed so it can later connect to n8n, CallTrackingMetrics, and FieldPulse. ## Required Intake Fields The agent should attempt to collect: * Caller name * Callback phone number * Whether the callback number can receive texts Suggested wording: “Is this a mobile number we can text if needed?” * City / ZIP where the vehicle or equipment is located * Vehicle or equipment description * Brief description of the issue * Urgency * Roadside / safety status * Existing customer vs. new caller if clear ## Call Classifications The agent should classify calls into categories such as: * Qualified service request * Incomplete intake / needs human review * Roadside or safety review * Existing customer follow-up * Non-service call / sales / spam * Out-of-area or maybe-out-of-area For incomplete calls, the agent should list the missing fields and mark the call as: **Needs Human Review — Incomplete Intake** ## Structured Output The test should produce structured output that can later be used by n8n. Example fields should include: * caller_name * callback_number * can_text_callback_number: true / false / null * city * zip * vehicle_or_equipment * issue_summary * urgency * roadside_or_safety_status * classification * incomplete_intake * missing_required_fields * human_review_required * transcript * summary * recording_or_call_link if available ## First Paid Test Deliverables For the first paid test, I expect: 1. Voice AI agent configured in my account. 2. Intake-only prompt / rules / behavior. 3. Guardrails to prevent diagnosis, pricing, scheduling, dispatching, or response-time promises. 4. 8–10 sample test calls. 5. Transcript and summary output. 6. Classification and missing-field handling. 7. Structured JSON output. 8. Email recap and SMS alert, or clearly mocked/sample alert output if full alert setup is not included. 9. Final prompt/configuration. 10. Setup notes. 11. Loom walkthrough explaining how the agent works. 12. Explanation of what I can safely edit later myself, such as script wording, approved responses, alert recipients, and minor rule changes. ## Future Expansion Later phases may include: * Connection to n8n * CallTrackingMetrics tracking number integration * FieldPulse-ready customer/job payloads * Better alert routing * More advanced review workflow * Miro flowchart update for the Voice AI portion These are not required for the first test unless specifically agreed. ## Ideal Candidate The ideal candidate has experience with: * Retell AI and/or Vapi * Voice AI prompt design * Intake call agents * Call classification * Webhooks * JSON outputs * n8n or Make * Twilio or SMS alert workflows * CRM or field service workflow integrations * Human-review routing * Clear documentation and Loom walkthroughs Direct experience with FieldPulse or CallTrackingMetrics is helpful but not required. ## Please Answer These Questions Start your reply with: **I can build the Voice AI intake agent.** Then answer: 1. Have you built voice agents using Retell, Vapi, or another voice AI platform? 2. Which platform do you recommend for this Phase 1 intake-only agent, and why? 3. How would you prevent the agent from diagnosing, estimating, scheduling, dispatching, assigning technicians, or promising response times? 4. How would you handle incomplete calls and missing required fields? 5. Can you produce structured JSON output for future n8n integration? 6. Can you include the field `can_text_callback_number: true / false / null`? 7. Can you send or simulate email recap and SMS alert output during the test? 8. What accounts/access would you need fro ---------- before starting? 9. Can the agent be built inside my account so I own the configuration? 10. What simple things would I be able to edit later myself? 11. Can you provide a Loom walkthrough at the end? 12. What fixed price and timeline would you quote for the first paid test? 13. Are you willing to send a short video reply before I make a final decision? ## Budget Please quote a fixed price for the first paid test. I am not looking for a full production system yet. I want a small controlled proof test first. If the test goes well, there may be additional work.

title: Social Media Manager
description: Social Media Manager — Role & Playbook Business: Website design for restaurants & local businesses Platforms: Instagram (primary), TikTok, Facebook The one job: Grow a relevant audience and turn it into DMs ? qualified leads ? paying clients. The Goal (read this first) Follower count is not the goal. The goal is DMs from restaurant owners that turn into paying clients. A 2,000-follower account full of local restaurant owners beats a 50,000-follower account full of random people every single time. At the same time this does not mean we do not want to grow the account the more followers we have the higher chance we can turn viewers and followers into leads. Every post must do one of three jobs: get discovered (Top of Funnel), build trust (Middle of Funnel), or drive a DM (Bottom of Funnel). If a post does none of these, don't post it. North-star metric: number of qualified DMs / leads passed to the owner per week. Secondary metrics: shares, saves, profile visits, follower growth (relevant followers only). Vanity metrics to ignore: raw likes, total followers without context. The Funnel — what to post and how much Use this mix as the default. Early on (under ~2k followers) lean heavier on Top of Funnel to grow reach; once the audience builds, shift more toward Middle and Bottom. Funnel tier % of posts Goal Metric that proves it worked Top (TOFU) ~50% Get discovered by people who don't know us Reach, shares, new follows Middle (MOFU) ~30% Prove we know our stuff Saves, comments, profile visits Bottom (BOFU) ~20% Turn warm followers into DMs DMs, link clicks, leads TOP OF FUNNEL — Viral Hooks, Broad Topics, Shares Purpose: reach strangers and get shared. These are broad, visual, and satisfying. No selling. Content types: Before/after redesigns of real restaurant sites "Redesigning a real local restaurant" series — pick a local spot with a bad site, rebuild it, reveal the transformation (this is the flagship format) Speed builds — sped-up "watch me build a restaurant site in 60 seconds" Broad relatable hooks about bad restaurant websites Hook bank (the first 1–2 seconds d ---------- everything): "This restaurant has amazing food and a website that's quietly killing their business." "I redesigned a local restaurant's website without them asking — here's what I changed." "POV: you Google a restaurant and this is their website." "Your restaurant's website is losing you customers every day. Here's proof." MIDDLE OF FUNNEL — Education, Frameworks, Saves Purpose: convince people who found us that we're the expert. Useful enough to save and send to a friend. Content types: Frameworks: "5 things every restaurant website needs (most miss #3)" Mistakes: "3 things wrong with most restaurant websites" Myth-busting: "Why relying on just a Facebook page is costing you money" Mini-explainers: online ordering, mobile speed, Google rankings — in plain English Hook bank: "5 things every restaurant website needs — most are missing at least two." "The 3-second test: if your site fails this, you're losing diners." "Stop relying on DoorDash for your online presence. Here's why." BOTTOM OF FUNNEL — Client Wins, Hard Pitches, DMs Purpose: turn warm followers into conversations. Direct, proof-driven, with a clear next step. Content types: Client wins / results: "We rebuilt [restaurant]'s site and their online orders went up — here's how." Transparent breakdowns: "Here's exactly what we did for this restaurant and what it cost." Direct offers: the comment-to-DM play (below) Hook bank: "We rebuilt this restaurant's website. Look at the difference." "Comment SITE and I'll send you a free preview of your restaurant's new website." "Want to see what your restaurant's site could look like? DM us 'WEBSITE'." The Weekly Posting Schedule Start at 5 posts/week (one per weekday), batched and scheduled a week ahead. Same vertical video gets posted to all three platforms — produce once, repurpose everywhere. Day Funnel Post Monday TOFU Before/after of a recent build Tuesday MOFU Educational framework / mistakes post Wednesday TOFU Redesign series — Part 1 (the bad site + "let's fix it") Thursday BOFU Client win / testimonial / results Friday TOFU Redesign series — Part 2 (the reveal) + soft CTA Rotate so that over two weeks you hit roughly 6 TOFU, 2 MOFU, 2 BOFU. To push more leads, swap a TOFU slot for a second BOFU once the audience is warm. The Social Media Manager's Exact Responsibilities Every week (planning — sent to owner for approval) Build the week's content calendar: what posts, which funnel tier, what day. Write the script and hook for each post (the spoken/on-screen lines). Write the caption and CTA for each post. Edit the raw footage the owner provides into finished vertical reels — captions, hook on screen, trending audio, tight pacing, strong first frame. Schedule every post across Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook . Every day Confirm the scheduled post went live on all three platforms. Engage in the first 60 minutes after posting — reply to every comment (this is when reach is d ---------- ). Reply to all DMs. Qualify lightly, log every lead in the tracker, and flag warm ones to the owner immediately. Spend 20–30 min commenting on target accounts — local restaurants, local business pages, food bloggers — to get the account in front of the right people. Every month Report: follower growth, top posts, saves/shares, DMs, leads passed. Note what worked and adjust the mix. How to Gain REAL Followers (not junk) Tag the restaurant in every redesign. When you feature a real local spot, tag them — they often reshare to their own followers (their customers and other owners). This is the single best source of relevant reach. Use local + niche tags: location tags for the city/region, plus restaurant/local-business hashtags. Skip giant generic tags. Reply to every comment and DM. Conversation tells the algorithm the content matters, and it builds real relationships. Be consistent. 5 posts every week beats 15 one week and none the next. Never buy followers, likes, or use engagement pods. It poisons your reach and brings zero buyers. The DM ? Lead Handoff (where the money is) This is the whole point. The conversion mechanic: BOTTOM-of-funnel posts end with a comment-to-DM call to action — "Comment SITE and I'll send you a free preview." Use a tool like ManyChat to auto-DM everyone who comments the keyword. This spikes engagement and drops a warm lead straight into the inbox. The SMM responds, asks 1–2 light qualifying questions (restaurant name, do they have a site now), and logs the lead in the tracker. Anyone who shows real interest gets flagged to the owner to close. Every DM is a potential client. The SMM's job is to start the conversation and hand the owner someone ready to talk. What the Owner Provides The SMM can't build the websites — that's you. Your weekly input is small: Raw footage: screen recordings of builds, before/after captures, the occasional talking-head hook. Batch it once a week into a shared folder. Approve the calendar the SMM sends. Close the warm leads the SMM hands you. Tools Scheduling:Google Calendar (or the free native Instagram/TikTok schedulers) Editing: CapCut Comment-to-DM automation: ManyChat Content calendar + lead log: Google Sheets or Notion (shared with the owner) The Rule That Keeps Everyone Honest Posts are judged by leads, not likes. A post with 200 likes and zero DMs failed. A post with 30 likes that produced two DMs from restaurant owners succeeded. Optimize relentlessly for the conversation, not the applause. We still do need followers, likes, and shares. It is not okay to not get leads or likes.

title: Landing Page Specialist
description: Landing Page Specialist (CRO-Focused) SALARY + PERFORMANCE BASED About the Role: We are looking for a Landing Page Specialist who understands that a landing page is not a brochure — it is a conversion system. Your job is to close the gap between ad click and purchase (or lead). You will own the design, copy, and continuous optimization of every landing page we run traffic to across Meta and Google campaigns. If you think a "good-looking" page is the goal, this is not the role for you. If you obsess over above-the-fold messaging, page speed, and why a visitor didn't convert, keep reading. What You Will Do: Design, build, and iterate high-converting landing pages for paid traffic (Meta, Google) across product pages, advertorials, lead gen pages, and VSLs. Ensure every page is tightly aligned to the ad that sent the visitor there — matching the hook, the angle, and the offer. Message match is non-negotiable. Write or closely collaborate on conversion copy: headlines, subheads, benefit stacks, objection handling, social proof, and CTAs. Run structured A/B and multivariate tests with clear hypotheses, proper statistical significance thresholds, and documented learnings. Optimize for page speed and Core Web Vitals, as both directly affect Quality Score on Google and conversion rates across all channels. Analyze heatmaps, session recordings, and funnel drop-off data (Hotjar, Microsoft Clarity, or equivalent) to identify friction points and prioritize fixes. Build landing page variants tailored to different funnel stages — top-of-funnel prospecting traffic requires a fundamentally different page than bottom-of-funnel retargeting traffic. Who You Are: Copy-First Thinker: You understand that design serves copy, not the other way around. You know that the headline is responsible for the majority of conversion outcomes and you treat it accordingly. Analytically Rigorous: You do not declare a test a winner based on gut feel or small sample sizes. You understand statistical significance and know when to call a test and when to let it run. Platform-Proficient: You are hands-on with at least one major page builder (Replo, GemPages, Pagefly, Unbounce, or Webflow) and can move fast without sacrificing quality. Funnel-Aware: You understand how the landing page fits into the broader acquisition funnel. You know what a Media Buyer needs from you and you can translate ad creative angles into page structure. Speed-Obsessed: You know that a 1-second delay in page load time can meaningfully reduce conversions and you treat performance optimization as a core responsibility, not an afterthought. Requirements: Portfolio of landing pages with documented conversion rate improvements (before/after data required — no portfolio without performance data will be considered). Proficiency in at least one page builder platform (Replo, GemPages, Pagefly, Unbounce, Webflow, or similar). Working knowledge of CRO principles: above-the-fold optimization, trust signals, social proof hierarchy, urgency/scarcity mechanics, and offer framing. Familiarity with heatmap and session recording tools (Hotjar, Microsoft Clarity, or equivalent). Basic understanding of how Google Ads Quality Score and Meta ad relevance diagnostics are affected by landing page experience. Excellent written English — you will be writing or editing copy directly. To Apply: Please include the phrase "Message Match First" at the top of your application. Along with your resume, attach or link to 2–3 landing pages you have built, and for each one, include the conversion rate before and after your involvement. Applications without performance data will not be reviewed.

To be incredibly clear: This is NOT a graphic design or video editing role. You will not be pushing pixels in Figma or editing timelines in Premiere. You are the architect of our ad account. Your job is to conduct deep market research, understand consumer psychology, develop high-converting direct response (DR) angles, and write airtight creative briefs for our design and editing teams. You will scour competitor ad libraries, mine customer reviews, read Reddit threads, and analyze TikTok comments to uncover hidden pain points and desires. - Angle & Concept Ideation: Develop original, direct response advertising angles. You must be able to explain why an ad won or lost. - Testing Roadmap Management: Build and manage our weekly creative testing pipeline, ensuring a consistent flow of fresh concepts, iterative variations of winning ads, and new format tests. Required Qualifications & Skills - Direct Response Mastery is Mandatory: You must have a deep, proven understanding of what makes a Meta ad convert. You know the anatomy of a winning ad, consumer psychology, and how to structure a pitch that drives immediate action. - Exceptional Copywriting & Scripting: Flawless written English. You must be able to write punchy, persuasive video scripts, ad copy, and headlines that resonate with a US-based consumer. - Data Literacy: You must be comfortable reading data. You know the difference between a creative problem (low hook rate) and a landing page problem (high CTR, low CVR), and you use that data to guide your next brief. - Proactive & Independent: You do not need to be micromanaged. You independently spot fatigue in our ad account, research what competitors are scaling, and pitch your own concepts. - Reliable Setup: High-speed internet connection (with a backup plan) and a reliable computer. Nice-to-Haves (Not Mandatory) - Prior experience strategizing for sleep-tech, health/wellness, or high-AOV premium home goods brands. - Familiarity with creative research and saving tools like Foreplay or Atria. How to Apply: If you are sharp, obsessed with consumer psychology, and ready to be the brains behind our Meta ad engine, please reply with: - A link to a portfolio or Google Drive folder containing 2–3 examples of creative briefs or scripts you have written that resulted in profitable ads, and the images/videos of those ads (if available).

Execute systematic keyword research (finding the 2-4 word "sweet spot") and ensure tight ad relevance and landing page alignment. Transition campaigns from Max Conversions/Manual CPC to tROAS/tCPA once proof of concept is established. Manage aggressive scaling strategies, monitoring key market dominance metrics like Search Impression Share, Absolute Top %, and Click Share. Maintain data integrity by properly segmenting branded vs. non-branded traffic and ensuring accurate tracking across the funnel. Who You Are: Deeply Analytical & Creative: You understand that media buying is now a blend of data analysis and creative strategy. You can brief creative teams based on performance data and psychological triggers/barriers. Systematic & Disciplined: You don't make emotional changes to campaigns. You respect learning phases (minimum 50-75 conversions on Meta) and scale budgets systematically (e.g., 20-30% bumps on Google). A Continuous Learner: You stay up-to-date with the bleeding edge of ad tech. You know why interest stacking is dead on Meta and how to properly structure a PMax campaign without cannibalizing search. Fluent in the Metrics that Matter: You look past vanity metrics. You speak the language of MER (Marketing Efficiency Ratio), Thumbstop Ratio, and true CPA. Requirements: Proven track record of managing profitable Meta and Google Ads campaigns (portfolio/case studies required). To Apply: Please include the phrase "Creative is Targeting" at the top of your application so we know you read this description. Along with your resume, please provide a brief summary of a time you successfully scaled a campaign using a creative-led strategy on Meta or a structured scaling approach on Google.

title: Lead Vendor Manager
description: # Lead Vendor Manager ## Job Overview We are looking for a strong, organized, and highly assertive **Lead Vendor Manager** to manage and grow our network of lead vendors. This person will be responsible for finding new vendors, onboarding them into our system, making sure they understand our rules, managing day-to-day vendor communication, handling disputes, tracking performance, and coordinating vendor payments. This role is not for someone passive. We need someone who can build relationships but also hold vendors accountable, enforce standards, and protect the company from bad traffic, poor-quality leads, compliance issues, and unnecessary payment disputes. The ideal candidate is confident, direct, detail-oriented, and comfortable dealing with high-volume vendor communication. ## Key Responsibilities ### Vendor Recruiting & Relationship Building * Actively search for and solicit new lead vendors. * Build relationships with vendors who can generate qualified insurance leads or transferred calls. * Explain our program, qualification standards, payment structure, and compliance rules. * Maintain a pipeline of potential vendors and follow up consistently. * Help evaluate whether new vendors are a good fit before they are approved. ### Vendor Onboarding * Guide new vendors through the onboarding process. * Make sure vendors are set up correctly in our vendor system. * Train vendors on call requirements, lead qualifications, transfer expectations, hours of operation, and compliance rules. * Confirm that vendors understand what is billable and non-billable before they begin sending traffic. * Work with internal tea ---------- mbers to make sure vendor setup, tracking, and reporting are accurate. ### Vendor Performance Management * Monitor vendor lead/call quality. * Track vendor volume, conversion quality, disputes, rejected leads, and payment trends. * Identify vendors who are sending low-quality traffic or failing to follow instructions. * Communicate clearly with vendors when performance needs to improve. * Recommend pausing, reducing, or terminating vendor relationships when needed. ### Dispute Management * Handle vendor disputes professionally and firmly. * Review disputed calls/leads against company rules and qualification standards. * Communicate payment decisions clearly to vendors. * Keep organized records of disputes, approvals, rejections, and final outcomes. * Protect the company from paying for unqualified or non-compliant leads. ### Vendor Payments * Prepare and review vendor payment reports. * Confirm billable leads/calls before payment is issued. * Coordinate weekly vendor payouts. * Track payment history and resolve payment-related questions. * Make sure vendors are paid accurately and on time when they meet requirements. ### Compliance & Quality Control * Ensure vendors follow company guidelines, including DNC requirements, transfer rules, scripting expectations, and call quality standards. * Watch for red flags such as misrepresentation, poor-quality transfers, recycled leads, non-qualified prospects, or compliance violations. * Escalate serious vendor issues quickly. * Maintain clean documentation around vendor rules, disputes, and performance. ## Ideal Candidate The ideal person for this role is: * Assertive and confident * Comfortable having difficult conversations * Not easily pushed around by vendors * Organized and detail-oriented * Strong at follow-up * Able to balance relationship-building with accountability * Comfortable enforcing rules and saying “no” * Fast-moving and proactive * Good with systems, spreadsheets, CRM tools, and reporting * Able to manage multiple vendors at once without losing track of details ## Required Skills & Experience * Experience managing vendors, lead providers, affiliates, call centers, or marketing partners preferred * Experience in insurance, pay-per-call, lead generation, sales, or performance marketing is a strong plus * Strong written and verbal communication skills * Strong negotiation and conflict-resolution skills * Ability to review data, reports, calls, and dispute records * High attention to detail * Comfortable working in a fast-paced sales environment * Ability to enforce rules without damaging productive relationships * Reliable, accountable, and self-managed ## Personality Fit This role requires someone with a strong personality. You must be able to push back when vendors are wrong, challenge questionable traffic, and enforce standards without needing constant direction. We want someone who is professional and respectful, but also firm, direct, and not afraid of confrontation when necessary. ## Success in This Role Looks Like * New vendors are consistently being recruited and onboarded. * Vendors clearly understand our expectations before sending traffic. * Disputes are handled quickly and fairly. * Payments are accurate and organized. * Bad vendors are identified and addressed quickly. * Good vendors are supported and encouraged to scale. * Internal teams have fewer vendor-related issues. * Lead/call quality improves over time. ## Compensation Compensation will depend on experience and role structure. This may include a base salary or hourly pay, with potential performance bonuses based on vendor growth, quality, and volume. ## How to Apply Please apply with your resume and a short note explaining your experience managing vendors, affiliates, lead sources, call centers, or similar relationships. Bonus points if you have experience in insurance, lead generation, pay-per-call, or performance marketing.

What we're looking for 2+ years writing direct-response briefs or scripts for DTC brands, ideally supplements, health, or beauty Native-level fluency in Meta ad creative — you can watch a UGC ad and tell us in 30 seconds why it's working Working knowledge of the awareness ladder, problem/solution/product awareness, and how to write for each stage Comfortable with research-heavy workflows: scraping reviews, lurking in Facebook groups and forums, finding the exact phrase a customer uses before they know what's wrong with them Organized. Our main business is a paddock-to-plate meat operation selling premium Wagyu and grass-fed beef direct to customers at markets and online. Alongside this we run cattle, produce hay, do contract farm work, and make a natural tallow-based skincare range. We need one reliable, long-term person to take ownership of our bookkeeping so we can focus on running the business. The role We have used QuickBooks for many years and have a lot of history in the file. We are staying on QuickBooks — we are NOT migrating to Xero. The first big job is a thorough cleanup and restructure of our existing QuickBooks Online file so that each of our enterprises reports clearly and our GST is correct. After that, you keep everything reconciled, accurately coded, and ready for our Business Activity Statements (BAS) and end-of-year tax. Important: BAS and tax documents are prepared by you and reviewed/lodged by the owner. You prepare; we review and lodge. What you will do • Clean up and restructure our existing QuickBooks Online file — review the chart of accounts, remove duplicates, fix inconsistent coding, and set up a clean, consistent structure (you would confirm the proposed structure with us before making major changes). • Set up each enterprise to report separately (meat, cattle, hay, contract work, skincare) using QuickBooks Classes (and Locations where helpful), so we can see income and expenses for each part of the business. • Process and reconcile all bank and credit card transactions across multiple accounts. • Handle Australian GST correctly. Most of our food/meat sales are GST-free, while many of our supplier purchases include GST that we can claim. You apply the right GST code to every transaction, and review and correct existing coding during the cleanup. • Prepare Business Activity Statements (BAS) and supporting documents for the owner to review and lodge. • Produce regular reports — profit & loss by enterprise, GST position, and cash position — so we can see how each part of the business is tracking. • Flag any errors, unusual transactions, or anything without supporting documentation, rather than guessing. We value someone who asks and flags rather than assumes. Must have • Solid hands-on experience with QuickBooks Online — including cleaning up and restructuring an established file, not just data entry. (This is essential. Please only apply if you are genuinely experienced in QuickBooks Online.) • Good understanding of Australian GST, including the difference between GST-free sales and GST-inclusive purchases, and BAS preparation. • Experience using QuickBooks Classes (and Locations) for separating and reporting on different parts of a business. • A bookkeeping or accounting qualification, with real experience keeping books for businesses. • Strong attention to detail and accuracy — this matters more to us than speed. • Reliable, responsive, and able to work independently to deadlines. Good written English, reliable internet, and your own computer. • Honesty and discretion handling confidential financial information. Nice to have • Experience with Australian clients and Australian BAS/tax. • Experience with multi-enterprise, farming, or primary-production accounts. • Payroll / STP experience. Why work with us • Long-term, stable role with room to grow your hours and responsibility. • Real ownership of the books — you run the system, not just data entry. • Flexible, deadline-based hours — we trust you to manage your own time and deliver. How to apply Applications that answer the questions below will be prioritised — it shows us you read the ad and helps us find the right person quickly. Please send: 1. Your CV / resume (pasted into your reply or attached through OnlineJobs.ph please — not a Google Drive link). 2. A short note on your QuickBooks Online experience — in particular, any file cleanups or restructures you’ve done. 3. Your experience with Australian GST and BAS. 4. Your hourly rate (in USD) and the hours per day you are available. And please answer these three quick questions in your application: • In QuickBooks Online, how would you set up the file so that income and expenses can be reported separately for several different parts of one business? • If a sale is GST-free but the supplier invoice for that product included GST, how do you treat each side in the books? • If you took over a messy QuickBooks file with duplicate accounts and inconsistent coding, how would you approach cleaning it up? description: College Career Pathways — College Counseling Practice Website Remote  •  Project-Based Overview We are looking for a skilled Webflow developer, website designer, and systems integrator to build a polished, professional website for College Career Pathways — a premium college counseling practice based in Katy, Texas. title: Executive Assistant
description: We are seeking a detail-oriented, proactive, and mission-aligned Executive Assistant to directly support the CEO. SCHEDULE * Part-time position * Monday through Friday * 12:00 PM to 4:00 PM EST * Opportunity for additional hours and expanded responsibilities as the organization grows LEADING PEOPLE You do not manage a team, but you represent the CEO's office in every interaction. Your professionalism, responsiveness, discretion, and follow-through reflect directly on the organization's leadership. You will be trusted with sensitive information, key relationships, organizational priorities, and executive communications. COMMUNICATION * Serve as the first point of contact for the CEO's office, including scheduling requests, email communications, and external inquiries. * Own the day-to-day management of the CEO's inbox, including prioritization, organization, drafting responses, and ensuring no communication falls through the cracks. * Partner closely with the organization's grant lead to support grant writing coordination, deadlines, submissions, and documentation. * Ensure internal teams receive clear communication regarding CEO priorities, decisions, and expectations. * Handle sensitive communications with confidentiality and sound judgment. * Document action items, commitments, and decisions from CEO meetings and ensure appropriate follow-up. STRATEGIC THINKING * Understand the CEO's priorities well enough to make informed decisions regarding scheduling, access, and time management. * Anticipate needs before meetings, events, deadlines, and major initiatives. * Monitor funding opportunities and trends relevant to the organization's mission and programs. * Identify administrative inefficiencies and recommend practical solutions that improve organizational effectiveness. ACCOUNTABILITY * Provide weekly executive briefings that include calendar updates, open action items, grant deadlines, and partnership status reports. * Ensure no grant deadline or compliance requirement is missed without advance notice and a documented plan. * Maintain accurate and current records within all tracking and CRM systems. * Ensure executive communications and follow-up expectations are consistently met. * Protect CEO capacity by owning responsibilities that should not require executive involvement. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS * Minimum of 3 years of experience as an Executive Assistant, Executive Coordinator, Project Coordinator, Administrative Operations Professional, or similar role. * Demonstrated experience directly supporting senior executives, founders, CEOs, or C-suite leadership. * Strong executive calendar management and inbox management experience. * Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, projects, and stakeholders simultaneously. * Experience working in a fast-paced, mission-driven, nonprofit, startup, or growth-oriented environment. * Strong organizational and project management skills. * Excellent written and verbal communication skills. * Experience using project management, collaboration, and CRM systems. * Comfortable working with AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, or similar platforms to support research, communication, organization, documentation, and administrative efficiency. * High degree of discretion, trustworthiness, professionalism, and sound judgment. * Strong alignment with the organization's mission of supporting underrepresented talent in technology. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS * Experience with grant research, grant writing, or nonprofit grant management. * Familiarity with federal, state, corporate, and foundation funding opportunities. * Experience coordinating cross-functional projects and organizational initiatives. * Experience supporting a founder, CEO, or executive leadership team. * Familiarity with HubSpot, Notion, Asana, Jira, Google Workspace, or similar platforms. IMMEDIATE HIRE OPPORTUNITY This is an immediate-hire opportunity for a candidate who can step into the role with confidence and professionalism. We are seeking someone who already understands the fundamentals of executive support and can quickly contribute to the success of the CEO and organization. HOW TO APPLY To be considered for this position, applicants must submit all of the following: 1. A current resume that includes complete employment history with start and end dates for each position. 2. A professional portfolio showcasing relevant work, accomplishments, projects, or case studies that demonstrate Executive Assistant, operations, project coordination, executive support, or organizational management experience. 3. A detailed introduction video that includes: * Your Executive Assistant experience * The executives or leaders you have supported * Examples of complex responsibilities you have managed * Why are you interested in this opportunity * Why do you believe you are a strong fit for this role 4. Must use at least 10 apply points to be considered. Applications that do not include all three required components will not be reviewed. Your experience with inventory, COGS, or cash-flow tracking 5. Your experience with Google Sheets or Excel 6. Your hourly or monthly rate 7. Your availability 8. description: We're a UK property company. We find rental property deals, analyse them, and either manage them ourselves or pass them to investors. There's a steady flow of potential deals coming in every day, and someone needs to go through them properly and tell us which ones are worth our time. It's careful, focused, repetitive work - and done well, it's one of the most important roles in the business, because everything we do starts with finding good deals and filtering out bad ones. We're looking for someone who is genuinely good at careful, detailed analysis, takes pride in getting it right, and wants a stable role they can settle into for the long term. Every day, you will: Find potential deals : Search specific Facebook groups and other online sources where property deals get posted. Filter them (first pass): Run each one against a clear set of pass/fail rules we'll give you. Most deals fail here - that's normal and correct. Your job is to kill the obvious "no" deals quickly so they never reach us. Analyse the survivors (deep dive): For the deals that pass the first filter, you'll do a proper analysis: pull the numbers, find comparable properties, check the competition, and fill out a deal analysis sheet we'll provide. Give a verdict: For each analysed deal, you'll give us a clear thumbs up or thumbs down - "this is a good deal" or "this isn't" - with your reasoning. We make the final call, but your verdict is what we act on, so it has to be sound. Keep everything organised: Log each deal in our system so nothing slips through the cracks. You will not be talking to landlords, negotiating, or closing deals. That's our side. Your job is the analysis and the verdict - and doing it accurately, every day, at good volume. You'll do well here if you: Can form a sound judgement on numbers. This is the heart of the job. You'll be d ---------- whether a deal is actually good, and we act on your verdict. We need someone who can look at the figures and think clearly about whether they really stack up - who can tell a genuinely good deal from one that's just been dressed up to look good. This is not copy-and-paste data entry. Stay consistent, so deal number 40 gets the same care as deal number 1. You don't get sloppy when you're tired or bored. You hit your daily targets without being chased, and a cleared list done correctly gives you genuine satisfaction. Catch the small things. A wrong comparable, a transposed number, a missing field - you notice it. In this work, small errors lead to wrong verdicts, so getting the details right the first time matters. Want this role for the long term. You're looking for a stable, steady job you can hold for years - not a stepping stone to something else. Have reliable power and internet. This work happens on a daily schedule, so you need a stable setup where you can work consistently without long outages. Please don't apply if you: Are looking for a short-term gig or a stepping stone while you pursue something else - studying full-time, planning to move abroad, building your own business on the side. This role needs your full focus and a long-term commitment. Get bored easily by repetitive, detail-heavy work. This job is the same careful process every day. If that sounds dull to you, you'll be unhappy here and so will we. You do not need any property or real estate experience - we'll train you on everything property-related. We're hiring for temperament and analytical ability, not property knowledge. How to apply There's a link below to complete the application form for this role. description: AI Recipe Video Clip Creator — Short-Form Food Content VA This is a great fit for an experienced VA who already has a job, steady income, or other clients, and wants a flexible side hustle with real long-term upside. This is not meant for someone who needs a high full-time salary immediately. It is paid from the beginning, but the bigger opportunity is participating in the upside through performance bonuses as the brand grows. The right person can keep their current job, work on their own schedule, and make a bet on something that has the potential to eventually make more money than their day job with less work. This is results-driven work for someone with long-term vision. We are looking for a detail-oriented VA to help create realistic AI-generated food clips for recipe reels, TikTok videos, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and other short-form social media content. Editing experience is a huge plus, especially if you already understand pacing, hooks, food visuals, short-form content, or what makes a clip feel polished and engaging. You will be helping turn high-protein comfort meal prep food recipes into realistic, appetizing video clips using tools like Higgsfield, Claude, and JSON-based prompting/workflows. We will teach the exact workflow, so you do not need to be an expert already. What matters most is that you have good taste, can follow instructions carefully, have a strong work ethic and can tell when food content looks realistic, delicious, and scroll-stopping. If you see this, write the word banana in your job title response. What You’ll Do You will create batches of AI video clips for each recipe, including things like: - Realistic cooking action shots - Ingredient prep clips - Sauce pours, cheese pulls, sizzling pans, plating shots, and meal prep container shots - High-quality clips that look appetizing, natural, and social-media ready - Prompting and adjusting clips using Claude, Higgsfield, and JSON instructions - Reviewing clips carefully and fixing details that look fake, messy, distorted, or unappetizing - Making edits when feedback is given The goal is to create short-form food videos that feel realistic, indulgent, high-protein, and visually delicious — not obvious AI slop. Tools You’ll Use - Higgsfield - Claude - JSON prompts / structured prompt formats - Google Drive or similar file organization - Social media reference videos for style and quality - If you can edit, probably CapCut and Primere Pro We will provide training, examples, recipes, prompts, and guidance. You Might Be a Great Fit If - You spend more time watching recipe videos than you’d like to admit. - You can instantly tell when a food video looks realistic and appetizing. - You enjoy experimenting with AI tools and learning new workflows. - You notice small details that other people miss. - You like flexible, output-based work that fits around your existing schedule. - You’re looking for a side hustle rather than another full-time commitment. - You already have VA, editing, social media, or content creation experience. - You care about making food look genuinely delicious, not just “technically correct.” - You are comfortable following structured instructions, prompts, and JSON formatting. - You are patient enough to regenerate or adjust clips until they look right. - You understand that tiny visual details matter: weird hands, fake steam, bad textures, unnatural sauce, distorted pans, or food that does not match the recipe. - You want to grow with a brand where strong performance can lead to higher pay, bonuses, upside opportunities, and more consistent work as sales increase. - You have long-term vision and understand that early-stage opportunities can grow into much bigger income once the brand gains traction. Requirements - **Strong attention to detail** - Good visual taste for food content - Ability to follow step-by-step instructions - Willingness to learn AI video tools - Comfortable using Claude or ChatGPT-style tools - Comfortable working with JSON or willing to learn - Reliable communication - Ability to deliver organized files on time - Interest in food, cooking, recipes, or short-form content - Editing experience is a huge plus - Must be able to accept feedback and make revisions Experience with AI video tools is helpful, but not required. We care more about your eye for quality, your ability to learn, and your ability to produce clips that look realistic, delicious, and usable for short-form content. And your ability to be consistent day in and day out to show up and perform and learn. Pay This is output-based freelance work and should be viewed as a flexible side hustle with growth potential. - $10 per completed batch of video clips per recipe - $5 for edits/revision batches. (Since it is AI clips, the editing is minimal. Adding text and music and trimming clips for a ~35 second video) - Pay includes the opportunity for performance bonuses - Strong performers may also participate in upside through bonuses - As sales and content performance increase, there will be opportunities for larger pay, higher bonuses, and more consistent work - The goal is for pay to increase significantly as the brand gains traction, especially for people who help build the system early and consistently deliver great work How to Apply Please send: 1. A short message about why you are interested 2. Any experience with AI tools, video editing, food content, VA work, or social media 3. 1–3 examples of food videos or short-form content you think look high-quality and explain why. If you don't have, explain a scenario where you were consistent even when the results did not show up how you wanted 4. Your availability each week 5. Confirm that you understand this is output-based side-hustle work with long-term upside: $10 per recipe clip batch and $5 for edits, with performance bonuses and upside opportunities as the brand grows Bonus points if you already watch recipe reels, TikToks, or food content and can explain what makes a clip look realistic, appetizing, and engaging. Send us your favorite food creator or a video you like.

title: Regulatory Compliance Officer
description: Australian compliance advisory firm, remote, part-time (room to grow) About ComplyEdge ComplyEdge is a boutique regulatory compliance and risk advisory firm based in Sydney, Australia. We help businesses across financial services, fintech, lending, real estate and professional services understand their regulatory obligations, manage compliance risk, and respond to regulators with confidence. Our work spans regulatory advisory, AML/CTF and financial crime, employment and industrial relations compliance, breach and i ---------- response, ongoing managed compliance, and compliance health reviews. We are growing, and I am looking for a reliable research and documentation assistant to support that work. The role You will help me with the research, analysis and document work that sits behind ComplyEdge’s advisory services. That means reading regulations and regulator guidance, turning them into clear summaries, and drafting compliance documents from templates and instructions. The work covers all of our service lines and every industry we support, so no two weeks look quite the same. This is a support role. I review all client-facing work before it is used, so you are never carrying regulatory advice on your own. What I need is someone careful, accurate and good with words. The details • Rate: AUD $5.00 per hour (approximately USD $3.30 per hour, depending on the exchange rate) • Hours: 15 hours per week to begin, with room to increase as we build a working rhythm and the workload grows • Around AUD $325 per month to start • Location: remote, Philippines-based independent contractor • Most work is asynchronous, though some overlap with Australian Eastern time for occasional check-ins is a plus What you will do • Research Australian regulatory developments, legislation and official guidance from bodies such as AUSTRAC, ASIC, the ATO, Fair Work and the OAIC, and summarise what matters • Analyse regulatory obligations and turn dense material into clear, structured briefing notes and summaries • Draft and format compliance documents, including policies, procedures, registers, checklists, templates and reports, working from instructions and existing templates • Support work across all of ComplyEdge’s service lines: regulatory advisory, AML/CTF and financial crime, employment and IR compliance, regulatory response and breach management, managed compliance retainers, and regulatory health reviews • Help keep our internal knowledge organised by tracking regulatory changes and maintaining document libraries • Support compliance work across the industries we serve, including financial services, fintech, lending and credit, real estate, and professional services How the work runs A few things matter to me, so I want to be clear about them upfront. • You work under my direction, and I review client-facing output before it goes anywhere. You provide research and drafting support, not regulatory advice. • Accuracy comes first. I expect work grounded in primary and official sources, with anything uncertain flagged rather than guessed. On regulatory detail, asking a question is always better than making something up. • You will handle confidential, client-sensitive information, and I expect complete discretion. What I am looking for • Strong written English. You can take a regulation or a guidance note and explain it clearly and correctly. • A background or real aptitude in compliance, law, regulation, audit, or a related field. • Genuine research skills and comfort reading legislation and official guidance. • Close attention to detail and a methodical way of working. • Reliability and the ability to manage your own time and hit deadlines without me chasing you. • Discretion with sensitive material. Nice to have • Familiarity with Australian regulatory frameworks such as AML/CTF, ASIC and AFSL requirements, Fair Work, or the Privacy Act • Exposure to financial services, fintech or lending compliance • Experience drafting policies, procedures or compliance registers • Confidence with everyday document and spreadsheet tools How to apply Please send me: 1. A short note (a few paragraphs) on your relevant experience and why this role suits you. 2. A brief writing task, so I can see how you research and write. In around 200 words and in plain English, explain one thing an Australian business must do under a regulatory obligation of your choice. Name the source you used. 3. Your weekly availability and any overlap you can offer with Australian Eastern time. 4. Confirmation that the rate works for you. Applications that skip the writing task will not be considered. This role has room to grow for the right person. If you take regulatory accuracy seriously and you write well, I would like to hear from you.

title: AI Social Media Content Creator
description: # AI Social Media Content Creator / AI Video Creator We are looking for a driven AI Social Media Content Creator who wants to become truly excellent at creating AI-generated short-form video content. This is not a “do the bare minimum and turn something in” role. We are looking for someone who takes pride in the details, cares about the final outcome, and wants to keep improving until the content is actually good. The right person for this role is creative, organized, diligent, and honest. You should care about doing clean work, following instructions, solving problems, and making content that performs better over time. ## About The Role You will help create AI-generated social media videos for different brands. The goal of the content is to get views, engagement, and attention from the right audience for each brand. You will be working with AI tools to help create short-form videos for platforms like Instagram Reels, TikTok, and similar platforms. This includes coming up with content ideas, writing or improving scripts, generating realistic AI images, turning those images into videos, editing the clips together, adding captions, creating hooks, and helping prepare the final video for posting. This role is for someone who wants to get really good at AI content creation, not someone who is just looking for an easy task list. ## What You’ll Be Doing You will help with tasks such as: Creating content ideas based on each brand’s ideal customer profile. Studying what kind of content performs well and using that to create better video ideas. Writing, organizing, or improving short-form video scripts and storyboards. Finding reference videos or images to help guide realistic AI-generated content. Creating AI-generated images using approved model photos, brand details, locations, outfits, and references. Making sure AI avatars look realistic, consistent, and natural over time. Creating image-to-video prompts for tools like Kling. Reviewing AI-generated clips and identifying what looks real versus what looks obviously AI-generated. Editing videos so they feel tight, natural, and engaging. Removing dead space, awkward pauses, bad clips, or anything that hurts the quality of the video. Adding hooks, captions, subtitles, and text that are easy to read on mobile. Making sure videos are formatted correctly for vertical social media. Posting content to the correct social media accounts when needed. Saving and organizing scripts, images, clips, and final videos in the correct folders. ## What We Care About Most We care about quality, effort, and character. We are not looking for someone who rushes through tasks, ignores details, or turns in messy work just to say it is done. We want someone who: Reads instructions carefully. Watches training videos when provided. Double-checks their work before submitting it. Asks smart questions when something is unclear. Takes ownership of the final result. Cares about making the video better, not just “finished.” Notices small details that make AI content look fake. Understands that clean organization matters. Has integrity and tells the truth if something went wrong. Is willing to learn, improve, and work harder to create a better outcome. ## This Is A Good Fit If You Are Someone who wants to become one of the best at creating AI social media content. Creative, but also organized. Detail-oriented and willing to follow a process. Comfortable learning new AI tools. Interested in social media, short-form video, marketing, hooks, and content strategy. Willing to study what works and improve over time. Good at spotting when something looks fake, awkward, or low-quality. Able to work independently without needing to be reminded about every detail. Proud of doing work the right way. The kind of person who would rather fix something than turn in something messy. ## This Is Not A Good Fit If You Only want easy copy-and-paste tasks. Skip instructions. Turn in unfinished or sloppy work. Use AI tools without reviewing the output. Say something is done when it clearly needs more work. Do not like feedback. Get annoyed by details. Need constant reminders to stay organized. Are not interested in improving your skill. Do not care whether the final video is actually good. ## Skills That Are Helpful Experience with AI image or video tools is helpful, but not required if you are a fast learner. Experience with any of the following is a plus: AI image generation. AI video generation. Short-form video editing. Instagram Reels or TikTok content. Writing hooks or captions. Social media content strategy. Canva, CapCut, Clipchamp, or other editing tools. ChatGPT prompting. Organizing creative files and project folders. Studying viral content and adapting it for different brands. ## The Standard We Expect Every video should be treated like it matters. That means the script should make sense, the visuals should match the concept, the AI model should look realistic, the video should be edited tightly, the captions should be readable, and the final version should feel like something a real person would stop and watch. You do not need to be perfect on day one. But you do need to care, learn fast, and take pride in improving. ## Why This Role Is Valuable AI content creation is becoming one of the most important skills in marketing. This role gives you the chance to get hands-on experience creating real AI-generated content for real brands. You will learn how to think about audience psychology, hooks, content ideas, AI visuals, video structure, editing, and posting. Over time, the goal is for you to become someone who can take a content idea and turn it into a strong finished video with minimal help. ## How To Apply Please apply only if you are serious about doing high-quality work. In your application, tell us: Why you want to get good at AI social media content creation. What makes you detail-oriented. An example of a time you worked harder than expected to create a better result. Any experience you have with AI tools, video editing, social media, or content creation. Why you believe integrity matters when working remotely. We are looking for someone who wants to grow into this skill, take ownership, and become excellent at creating AI social media content.

This is the strategic-creative seat that turns raw market signal, customer voice, and the competitive landscape into a differentiated product concept brief — the document that our research, sourcing, brand management, and design teams all build against. To be clear about what this role is not: you won't run the product research scoring process, manage the catalog or listing operations, write listing copy, produce creative assets, or negotiate with manufacturers. Dedicated specialists own each of those. Your job is to walk into a category that research has already validated and produce the differentiated concept brief — positioning, USP architecture, naming, size and variation mix, packaging direction, listing angle, and brand voice — that turns "another bedding product" into something obviously distinct from the closest competitors. The role is roughly 60?ep concept work, 25% cross-functional partnership and decision-making, and 15% continuous-improvement direction on existing products. If your passion is manufacturing, design execution, or running ads, this isn't the right fit. If you thrive on synthesizing disparate signals into a sharp, defensible product offer — and then watching that brief ship through a fast-moving execution team — read on. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Concept Briefs for New Launches (?60% of your time) Take the handoff once a category is validated by research, and produce the locked concept brief before sourcing begins. Define the differentiated offer: USP architecture, positioning, naming, size and variation mix, packaging direction, listing angle, brand voice, and a clear statement of what the concept is not. Pull and synthesize primary research — competitor review corpora, competitor listings, search-query data, trend signals, and internal performance patterns. Build and defend the differentiation hypothesis with written evidence, not opinion. Run each locked brief through a structured review with brand management, design, and sourcing before handoff. Hold the line on commoditized concept submissions, escalating only when there's a genuine dispute. Cross-Functional Partnership & Decision-Making (?25% of your time) Weekly sync with the product research team on pipeline scoring and category prioritization. Weekly sync with the catalog manager on listing-strategy handoff and variation-expansion decisions. Weekly sync with the creative director on visual identity briefs and concept-to-creative translation. Bi-weekly sync with brand management on existing-product performance signals that may call for re-conceptualization. As-needed coordination with sourcing on capability constraints and substitution decisions. D ---------- which existing products are candidates for re-concept versus incremental tuning, and brief the work. Escalate to the CEO only what genuinely requires it — product kills, major positioning shifts, brand-architecture moves. You own everything below that line. Cross-Functional Coordination Collaborate with PPC specialists on campaign strategy, bid optimization, and budget allocation aligned with brand-level goals Work with the inventory and logistics team to manage DOS (Days of Supply), prevent stockouts on hero SKUs, and mitigate LTSF (Long-Term Storage Fee) exposure Coordinate with product development on listing improvements, packaging changes, and product enhancements driven by review analysis and competitive gaps Partner with the creative team on A+ content, image optimization, and video content development Communicate action plans with clear ownership, deadlines, and success metrics. No open-ended initiatives Continuous-Improvement Direction (?15% of your time) Identify existing products whose performance has plateaued, and propose re-conceptualization rather than endless incremental tuning. Build the re-concept brief for relaunch when the concept — not the execution — is the bottleneck. Document the concept patterns that win and lose, turning the work into institutional memory rather than personal craft. Maintain a concept library and a competitive-concept teardown archive. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR Required Experience 6+ years total in product strategy, product marketing, product innovation, or category management at private-label or own-brand e-commerce companies. At least 3 years specifically in private-label e-commerce, consumer brand strategy, or category management. (Purely agency-side experience won't be a fit for this role.) Direct experience building product concepts that went to manufacture and launch — you'll be asked to reference launched products whose concept you owned. A demonstrated ability to read competitive landscapes and produce differentiated angles. We'll ask for written examples. Strong writing skills — your output is briefs, not pitches. We test this directly in the skills assessment. Deep comfort reading Amazon listings, customer review corpora, competitor ASINs, and search-query data, and translating all of it into a concept brief. Genuine AI fluency in your daily workflow — comfort with tools like ChatGPT and Claude, AI image tools for visual concepting, and a track record of integrating AI into a real research workflow. Fluent written and verbal English. This is a CEO-facing role, and writing is the core unit of work. Strong project-management discipline and comfort with async-first written communication (we use tools such as ClickUp, Notion, and Slack). Proven leadership and team management experience - you’ll own cross-functional decisions from day one, and this seat is built to grow into leading a team. Strong Preferences Experience with bedding, sleep, home textiles, or an analogous high-subjectivity category (apparel, beauty, supplements, premium home goods). Experience at a private-label brand that scaled meaningfully (for example, from $5M to $50M+ in annual revenue) with you owning concept work for at least three launched products. A brand-naming portfolio — three or more launched product or line names you originated, with the rationale behind them. Physical packaging concept experience, not just digital. Working knowledge of Amazon's brand-content surfaces (Brand Story, A+ and Premium A+ content) as places a concept gets expressed. Nice to Have Direct knowledge of bedding construction: weave types, GSM math, fabric blends, color-trend cycles. Comfort reading search-query-performance data and ranking reports and translating them into concept-level implications. TikTok Shop concept-work experience. A background as a brand manager or senior product marketer who moved into pure concept and innovation work. WHAT YOU'LL GET Competitive salary based on experience A fully built system to walk into: an established product research pipeline and scoring framework, a launch pipeline already in flight, master keyword lists, a competitive-intelligence database, and detailed per-product source-of-truth files. You inherit structure, not a blank page. An AI research and synthesis partner from day one: AI-powered operational tools that deliver daily analytics, weekly summaries, competitor intel, listing-performance signals, and structured frameworks for concept evaluation. A 90-day onboarding playbook to ramp from zero context to shipping locked concept briefs. Direct CEO access for decisions above your authority level — a clear escalation path with no middle-management bureaucracy. A growing company: we're expanding from Amazon into TikTok Shop and early-stage DTC Shopify, opening new categories and channels. A clear growth path: as the portfolio scales, this role can evolve into Head of Product Strategy, leading a team of researcher-strategists. Fully remote, with employee discounts across our brands. Work from anywhere with strong English fluency and meaningful overlap with US working hours. title: Project Reviewer
description: Project Reviewer - Civil Site Design & Utilities Modern Engineering Solutions, LLC | Fully Remote - Global Opportunity You'll Be Perfect For This Role If: You're an engineering professional with 4-8 years of experience, and you're frustrated with how most firms handle quality control. Maybe you're tired of: ? Being rushed through reviews to meet arbitrary deadlines ? Finding the same mistakes repeatedly because no one learns from feedback ? The "just get it approved" mentality that treats QA as an afterthought ? Being stuck in an office when the work doesn't require it ? You're open to using modern tools (including AI) to streamline documentation, and you understand that protecting time for thorough review is how you catch problems before they become expensive failures. What We Believe Here's how we run things differently: ? We Focus on Getting It Right, Not Getting It Done Fast Your value isn't how many plan sets you can rush through—it's the problems you catch before they reach clients or construction. A review that prevents a $200K construction error or catches a code violation before permit submittal? That's worth more than logging extra review hours. ? Quality Can't Be Rushed We give reviewers the time they need to do thorough work. Time-to-delivery matters, but not at the expense of catching critical errors. We treat quality review as an engineering constraint, not an afterthought. ? Deep Work Over Busy Work We protect your calendar. No back-to-back meetings. No "quick syncs" that break your concentration. Reviewers need uninterrupted time to systematically work through designs—that's where you catch the subtle problems that matter. ? AI Handles the Grunt Work We use AI for formatting review comments, tracking standard items, and generating markup templates. You still do all the technical judgment and critical review—AI makes mistakes—but it frees you up to handle 10 projects instead of 2. ? We Grow Carefully We're not chasing debt-fueled growth. We'd rather expand slowly with cash reserves so we can maintain quality standards and give reviewers adequate time for thorough work. ? We Keep Learning "That's how we've always done it" isn't good enough. We're constantly refining our review processes, learning from mistakes, and getting better at catching problems early. What You'll Do Conduct systematic quality assurance reviews of civil site designs and utility infrastructure: ? Review commercial site development plans including grading, drainage, paving, and utility layouts for technical accuracy and code compliance ? Analyze plan sets, stormwater calculations, and hydraulic analyses to identify errors and improvement opportunities ? Verify compliance with municipal design standards, state regulations, and local development criteria ? Conduct constructability reviews to ensure designs can actually be built as intended ? Prepare detailed review summaries with clear, actionable feedback ? Work directly with Project Managers and Engineers to resolve technical issues ? Review water, sewer, and stormwater system designs for functionality and compliance ? Maintain and update quality control checklists and review procedures ? Support permit application reviews to ensure regulatory compliance ? Help junior engineers learn from review feedback to improve future designs What You Need Required: ? title: Senior Accountant
description: About the role Cottonwood Acquisitions is a small-business operator group with nine portfolio companies across the US and Canada. We're hiring a remote senior accountant to lead day-to-day accounting across three of our businesses: Pacific Register (manufacturer of decorative HVAC registers, Oxnard CA USA), Total Restoration (restoration and mitigation services, Penticton BC Canada), and Marine Systems (manufacturer of decorative HVAC grilles and thermoformed components for yachts, Asheville, NC, USA). This is a hands-on senior accounting role reporting directly to the CEO. The right hire takes pride in clean financial statements, accurate bank reconciliations, and well-supported audits. Initial scope is three entities. What success looks like The single most important outcome is to own the preparation of monthly financial statements and quarterly bank reporting. Within 90 days we want this hire owning the monthly close, producing clean GAAP-quality financial statements with management commentary, and serving as the day-to-day liaison with our external auditors at year-end. Day-to-day responsibilities Own the monthly close across three entities, hands-on. A representative slice of what this involves: bank reconciliations for cash, posting customer payments across credit card / PayPal / ACH channels, multi-state sales tax filings, full bank and credit card reconciliations, journal entries and accruals, intercompany allocations between US and Canadian entities, customer advance reclassifications, and AP/AR oversight. Manage the bookkeepers at each of the businesses, coach them on how to improve processes and identify technology to streamline processes. Prepare monthly three-statement financial packages (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow statement) with management commentary. Calculate quarterly bank covenant compliance against existing credit agreements (DSCR, leverage ratios, fixed charge coverage, working capital tests). Manage year-end external audit support across all three entities — prepare PBC schedules, respond to auditor requests, drive resolution of open items. It will take some time to understand the businesses and we would like to see the candidate embark to understand the 3 businesses and build a FAQ document of the people at the businesses, what their roles are and what you learn about the businesses. Then when there are slower periods in the role, we would like to see the creation of process documentation to professionalize our accounting processes. Must-haves CPA equivalent license required Experience having worked full time for an English speaking business in the past is required 6–12 years accounting experience, including ownership of monthly close Strong written and spoken English Multi-entity accounting experience QuickBooks Desktop and Sage 50 Canada experience is helpful, but not required US or Canadian SMB client experience preferred Comfortable preparing three-statement financial packages independently Hands-on orientation — "no task too small" Strong nice-to-haves Big 4 / SGV / SyCip background (audit experience preferred) Manufacturing or services industry experience Experience supporting acquisitions or year-end audits Work setup Fully remote with some Bridge overlap with USA Pacific Time. Weekly check-in call. After the transition period, we expect ad hoc calls outside of the designated hours to be uncommon — typically no more than 1–2 per week, often less. Email and Messages for everything else. Camera-on during calls. Ideal candidate profile The person who's right for this role is a mature senior accountant who takes pride in precision work and clean books. They've outgrown their current seat at a local firm or BPO client and want a longer-term home with a growing US business. They love a clean reconciliation. They write well in English. They're comfortable being the most senior accountant on the team but unbothered by hands-on detail work — they understand that a clean balance sheet doesn't reconcile itself. They are looking for a stable, dignified, longer-term role where their craft is valued and the work is interesting enough to grow into. Work Location: Remote

title: Virtual Assisstant

The ideal candidate must be fluent in English and French, have strong communication skills, and understand property management procedures in both Ontario and Quebec, including tenant notices, leases, rent collection, maintenance follow-ups, and documentation. The TAL handles lease-related matters such as rent increases, repossessions, and landlord/tenant disputes, while Ontario’s Residential Tenancies Act provides the framework for residential tenancies, including rent increases and evictions. Key Responsibilities The Bilingual Virtual Assistant will be responsible for: Managing daily email communication with tenants, owners, contractors, and team members in both English and French. Answering tenant inquiries professionally and escalating urgent matters to the property manager. Coordinating maintenance requests, following up with contractors, requesting quotes, and updating tenants and owners. Preparing and sending notices, letters, reminders, and property-related communications in English and French. Assisting with lease administration, renewals, rent increase notices, tenant onboarding, and move-in/move-out coordination. Updating property management software with tenant information, charges, maintenance notes, lease details, documents, and communication records. Following up on unpaid rent, payment confirmations, utility bills, invoices, and owner-related accounting requests. Organizing documents, invoices, quotes, inspection photos, reports, and property files. Assisting with leasing tasks, including responding to rental inquiries, scheduling showings, screening applicants, collecting documents, and preparing lease files. Tracking deadlines for renewals, notices, maintenance work, inspections, and tenant requests. Supporting Ontario and Quebec property-management workflows, including LTB/TAL-related documents and timelines. Preparing clear summaries and updates for management, owners, and internal meetings. Required Qualifications Fluent in English and French, written and spoken. Previous experience as a virtual assistant, administrative assistant, property management assistant, or leasing coordinator. Property management experience in Ontario and Quebec is strongly preferred. Knowledge of residential leases, tenant notices, rent collection, maintenance coordination, and tenant communication. Familiarity with Ontario LTB and Quebec TAL processes is a strong asset. Strong writing skills and ability to prepare professional email s, notices, and reports. Excellent organization, follow-up, and time-management skills. Comfortable working remotely and independently. Strong attention to detail and ability to document all communication properly. Ability to handle tenant issues professionally and calmly. Experience using property management software such as Buildium, AppFolio, DoorLoop, Yardi, or similar is an asset. Proficient with Google Drive, Gmail, Google Sheets, Microsoft Office, and DocuSign. Ideal Candidate The ideal candidate is proactive, reliable, detail-oriented, and comfortable handling multiple properties and priorities at the same time. They must be able to communicate professionally with tenants, owners, contractors, and team members while keeping accurate records of every request and follow-up. This person should understand that property management requires strong documentation, fast follow-up, and clear communication, especially when dealing with maintenance, rent collection, lease renewals, tenant complaints, and legal notices. Work Schedule Remote position. Monday to Friday availability preferred. Occasional urgent follow-ups may be required depending on tenant or maintenance issues. Ontario and Quebec business-hour availability is preferred. How to Apply Please send your resume and a short message explaining your property management experience in Ontario and Quebec, your level of English and French, and any property management software you have used. Subject line: Bilingual Virtual Assistant – Property Management Application Short Version for Job Posting Ottawa Prime Properties is hiring a bilingual Virtual Assistant with property management experience in Ontario and Quebec. The ideal candidate must be fluent in English and French, highly organized, experienced in property management, and comfortable working remotely with tenants, owners, contractors, and internal team members.

title: B2B Cold Caller
description: We're hiring an experienced cold caller to book 15-30 minute discovery calls with home service business owners (garage door repair, tree trimmers, spas) for our AI voice agent. To apply (applications missing any of these will not be reviewed) A 45-60 second voice recording reading the sample opener and pitch below. Read it like you're actually making the call, not like you're reading aloud. Sample opener: "Hi, this is [name] calling from Good AiDeas. The reason for my call is we're working with garage door companies across the US, and we've been finding that most of them are losing 20-30 calls a month to voi cemail and afterhours calls not being picked up or returned. We built an AI receptionist that answers those calls 24/7 and books the job straight into the your team's calendar. Do you have 60 seconds for me to explain how it works?" Sample pitch (1-2 sentences): "It's a voice AI receptionist. Not a chatbot. It sounds like a real person, takes the caller's info, qualifies the job, and books it. It costs a fraction of a receptionist and never sleeps. Most of our customers are booking 10-20 extra jobs a month within the first 30 days." And in one sentence: who did you call in your last cold calling role, what were you booking, and what was your booking rate (per hour, per day, or per week. Provide your hourly rate and weekly availability. Confirm your time zone and that you can work US business hours. I'm in the US EST (New York) timezone.
