description: Type: Full-time · 100% Remote · Long-term (we want someone to grow with us for years) Salary: ?40,000/month (with a raise at 90 days based on performance) · Paid bi-weekly Hours: 40 hrs/week, with at least 40 hours overlapping Sydney, Australia Start: With a paid 2-week trial before we commit to the full salary --- About the role We're a small, fast-moving data/intelligence company. We track people who do high-quality technical work in open source — engineers who actively contribute code to public projects. Your job is to take a contributor we've identified (you'll usually have a name and/or email plus a link to their code activity) and confirm who they really are across the open web: their personal website, professional profiles, publications, and public contact details. This is careful detective work — not bulk scraping. We care far more about being right than being fast. One confidently wrong match is worse to us than ten honest "I couldn't confirm this." If you take pride in getting things exactly right and you enjoy a good puzzle, you'll like this job. What you'll do day to day - Start from a developer's email and/or name plus links to their public code activity. - Search the open web to find and confirm the same person: personal/portfolio site, GitHub/GitLab, LinkedIn, Google Scholar, arXiv or other publications, blog, X/Twitter, conference talks, university or company pages. - Cross-check evidence so you're confident it's genuinely the same person (matching email , reused username, photo, bio, employer, location). - Record each finding in our tool: every link, what type it is, and how confident you are, with the reason why. - Flag hard cases (common names, conflicting evidence) for review instead of guessing. - Keep your work organized, sourced, and easy for us to audit. You're a great fit if you - Are genuinely good at online research / people-finding and enjoy the hunt. - Have strong English reading comprehension and write clear, short notes. - Are extremely detail-oriented and honest about uncertainty — you say "not sure" when you're not sure. - Are comfortable around developer/tech websites (GitHub, Stack Overflow, etc.), even if you're not a programmer. - Are reliable, self-managing, and consistent over the long term. - Handle people's personal information responsibly and confidentially — we work only with publicly available info and we respect privacy. Nice to have (not required) - Experience as a VA, lead-generation researcher, recruiter/sourcer, or data researcher. - Familiarity with Google Sheets, Boolean search, LinkedIn, or Google Scholar. - Any exposure to software/tech communities. Compensation & growth - ?40,000/month full-time after the trial. - Paid 2-week trial first (same hourly rate) so we both make sure it's a fit. - Performance review and raise at 90 days, tied to accuracy and consistency. - Long-term, stable role with training — we're hiring someone to stay. Requirements: Reliable computer, stable internet, and a quiet space to record a short audio clip. --- How to apply (read carefully — most applicants will be rejected for skipping a step) We receive a lot of AI-generated and copy-paste applications. The steps below are designed so a real researcher passes easily and a bot fails. Do all five, in order — applications missing the recording, the screenshot, or the keyword are deleted unread: 1. Start your message with this exact phrase: CONTRIBUTOR-7741. Then, on the next line, finish this sentence in your own words (1–2 sentences, your real opinion): "The hardest part of confirming someone's identity online is…" 2. Mini-task. Find out who the GitHub user matklad really is, and tell me: - (a) Their full real name. - (b) The two specific links you used to confirm it — paste the actual URLs — and for each, the one detail on that page that ties it to the same person. - (c) One thing you found this month — their most recent public post, commit, talk, or release — with the date and a link. - (d) One link you ruled OUT — something that looked like them but wasn't — and why. - (e) Your confidence (High / Medium / Low) and the reason. 3. A screenshot of one of the pages from step 2, taken on your own screen (we'd like to see your browser tabs / clock in it). 4. A 60–90 second screen recording (Loom is free) of you doing any one search step, talking through what you're looking at, out loud in English. Audio required. This is the most important step. 5. At the very end, answer in one line: "What did you have for breakfast today, and what's the weather like where you are right now?" We reply to everyone who completes all five steps. We're hiring for the long term and will invest in training the right person.

title: # AI Content Workflow & Editorial QA Assistant
job_title: # AI Content Workflow & Editorial QA Assistant
description: # AI Content Workflow & Editorial QA Assistant ## About the role We’re looking for someone to help manage and quality-check our AI-assisted content workflow. This role is not about writing every post from scratch. Most of the content will already be generated using our approved AI prompts, frameworks, and systems. Your job is to take that AI-generated content through the correct workflow, apply the required checks, and act as the final human reviewer before the content moves forward. The main goal is to make sure each post sounds clear, natural, useful, and human — not robotic, generic, or obviously AI-generated. ## What you’ll do You will take AI-generated content and move it through our internal workflow. You will follow a clear step-by-step process for reviewing, checking, and improving each post. You will use our prompts, tools, and editorial guidelines to refine content where needed. You will act as the final human checker before posts are approved for the next stage. You will review each post to make sure it does not sound “AI-ified.” You will check for generic phrasing, robotic tone, repetitive structures, unnatural wording, and over-polished AI-style language. You will make light edits where needed to improve tone, flow, clarity, and readability. You will preserve the original idea and structure wherever possible, rather than rewriting everything unnecessarily. You will flag posts that need a deeper rewrite or strategic review. You will make sure posts feel aligned with the intended voice, audience, and content purpose. ## What we’re looking for We’re looking for someone with strong editorial judgment, a good ear for natural writing, and the ability to follow a repeatable content process. You do not need to be a senior copywriter, but you do need to understand when writing sounds awkward, generic, robotic, or too obviously AI-generated. You should be comfortable working with AI-generated drafts, improving them efficiently, and knowing when to make small edits rather than overworking the content. ## You’ll be a good fit if you can: Follow a structured workflow without skipping steps. Spot when a post sounds too much like AI. Make AI-generated writing sound more natural and human. Improve content without changing the original meaning. Keep edits light, purposeful, and practical. Understand the difference between polishing, humanising, and rewriting. Work through multiple pieces of content with consistency and attention to detail. Apply feedback and internal guidelines accurately. ## Key responsibilities Move AI-generated content through the agreed workflow. Apply editorial checks to each post. Review posts for AI-style language and tone. Humanise wording where needed. Improve clarity, rhythm, and readability. Check that the post still reflects the original prompt, message, and intended outcome. Flag weak posts, unclear ideas, or anything that needs further input. Prepare content for the next stage of review, scheduling, or client delivery. ## Skills required Strong attention to detail. Good writing and editing instincts. Ability to follow a process. Comfort using AI tools and content platforms. Ability to identify generic or robotic language. Good understanding of natural, conversational writing. Ability to make light edits without over-rewriting. Reliability and consistency when reviewing content at volume. ## Nice to have Experience reviewing social media content. Experience working with LinkedIn posts. Experience using ChatGPT, Claude, or other AI writing tools. Experience with content workflows, editorial QA, or agency content production. Understanding of tone-of-voice guidelines. ## What success looks like Content moves smoothly through the workflow. Posts are checked carefully before moving forward. AI-generated drafts sound more natural, specific, and human. Posts do not feel generic, robotic, or obviously AI-written. The original message is preserved while the quality is improved. Weak content is flagged rather than passed through. The final output feels polished, clear, and ready for review or publishing. ## Role summary This role is ideal for someone who is organised, detail-oriented, and has a strong instinct for natural writing. You’ll be working with AI-generated content, but the value you bring is human judgment: knowing what sounds real, what sounds forced, and what needs to be adjusted before it goes out.

description: We are looking for a detail-oriented research specialist to help us identify and compile independent music artists who meet a specific set of criteria. This is a research and data collection role. You will not be doing outreach — your job is to find the right artists, verify they meet our requirements, and deliver clean, organized lead reports. Quality is everything in this role. We do not want volume. We want accuracy. Every lead you submit should be one you have personally verified against the full checklist. Scouts who consistently submit unqualified leads will not continue with us. What You'll Be Doing: Searching for independent music artists across YouTube and Spotify who match our target profile. Verifying each artist against a detailed checklist before submitting. Collecting specific data points for each artist and organizing them into clean reports. Submitting leads in batches on a regular schedule with notes on why each artist qualifies. Target Artist Profile: Genres we are focused on: Phonk (all types including drift, slowed and reverb, Brazilian phonk), Synthwave, Retrowave, Electronic, Lo-fi, Ambient, and similar instrumental or electronic music styles. Priority regions: Russia, Kazakhstan, Ukraine, Georgia, Armenia, Belarus, and other Eastern European and CIS countries. Latin America and Asia are also welcome. Any country is acceptable but the listed regions are highest priority. Minimum size requirements: At least 500K monthly listeners on Spotify, OR multiple tracks with 2 million or more views on YouTube. Distribution: Artists must be on DistroKid, TuneCore, standard Amuse, Routenote, or self-distribution. Do not submit artists on The Orchard, Black 17, Chillhop, Create Music Group, Believe, or any major label. What to Look For: Original music only — no covers, no slowed and reverb versions of mainstream hits. Active YouTube channel with consistent uploads and views. Independent-looking artists with no obvious label affiliation. User-generated content presence — search the artist's song titles on YouTube and TikTok and note how many non-official videos are using their music. This is an important signal and should be included in every report. Verification Process — Follow This Exactly: Step one: Check the YouTube video description. Look at the "Provided to YouTube by" line to identify the distributor. Look at the copyright line — "Copyright Control" or the artist's own name is a green flag. Any third-party company name is a red flag. Step two: Search the artist name and song titles in the ASCAP and BMI public databases. If nothing comes up, that is a strong green flag. If a third-party publisher appears, do not submit the artist. Step three: Check Spotify credits on the artist's top tracks. Look for any publisher or admin name listed. Any artist with a visible third-party publisher or admin in their credits. What to Submit for Every Artist: Artist name. Main YouTube channel link. Spotify artist link if available. title: Senior Cold Email Strategist (Experts Only)
description: We are hiring a cold email expert — someone who has spent years doing this at a high level and has the numbers to prove it. If you are still learning, this is not the role for you. We need someone who can walk in, build the entire system from scratch, and consistently deliver results without being managed. We are a founder-led company with no existing cold email infrastructure. You will own everything from technical setup to copywriting to optimization. Leads will be provided to you — your job is to build the system that converts them into replies and booked conversations. Our team will not be guiding you. You will be guiding us. You Must Have: Minimum 3–5 years of dedicated cold email experience — not general marketing, not social media. Cold email specifically. A consistent, documented track record of 5%+ positive reply rates (not open rates — actual interested replies) across multiple campaigns. Experience running campaigns across multiple industries and ICPs — not just one niche. Deep technical knowledge: you have personally configured SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and managed domain and inbox health from scratch many times. Experience managing high-volume infrastructure across multiple domains and inboxes with proper sending rotation. Strong enough copywriting ability that your email s get mistaken for handwritten outreach — not templates. Experience diagnosing and fixing deliverability problems — you've been in spam before and you know exactly how to get out. What You'll Build & Run: Infrastructure: Full domain and inbox strategy covering quantity, naming, and age strategy. DNS setup with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configured correctly from day one. Inbox warming protocol and ongoing deliverability monitoring. Sending platform setup and configuration using Instantly, Smartlead, or equivalent. Copywriting: Multi-step sequences written to generate replies, not just opens. Subject lines, openers, CTAs, and follow-up timing — all tested and optimized. Copy adapted to different audiences as our targeting evolves — we work with independent music artists and YouTube creators, so comfort with the creator economy is a strong plus. Ongoing A/B testing with clear documentation of what moved the needle and why. Reporting: Weekly performance reports covering open rate, reply rate, positive reply rate, and meetings booked. Plain-language analysis of what's working and what needs to change. Honest assessment — if the copy or targeting angle is the bottleneck, we expect you to say so directly. Non-Negotiable Requirements: You must be able to provide specific campaign data including industry, offer, reply rate, and outcome. Vague answers disqualify immediately. You must have worked with at least 3 different sending platforms — not just one tool. Fluent written English is mandatory — you are writing email s to English-speaking decision-makers, creators, and artists. You must be comfortable owning results, not just activities. We do not measure success by email s sent. You Are Probably NOT a Fit If: Your experience is mostly internal email marketing or newsletters. You have only run campaigns in one or two industries. You cannot share reply rate data from past campaigns. You need significant direction or hand-holding. Your best campaigns averaged below 4% positive reply rate. Application Requirements — All Four Are Mandatory: Incomplete applications will not be reviewed. First, share 3 specific campaigns with the offer, target audience, sending volume, and positive reply rate. Screenshots or reports are strongly preferred. Second, provide a brief technical walkthrough describing how you would set up a brand new cold email system from scratch covering domains, inboxes, warming, DNS, and sending platform. This should take you two minutes to write if you know your craft. Third, write a 3-step cold email sequence for the following scenario: a platform that helps independent music artists and YouTube creators get brand deals and monetize their content, targeting the creators themselves. Show us what you can actually write. Fourth, list the tools you use for sending, email verification, and deliverability monitoring, and explain why you prefer each one.

description: Job Title: Python/Flask Developer – API Integration (Tripletex) & Custom Financial Dashboard Modules ?About the Project: We are a real estate development and construction company looking for an experienced Python developer to finalize an automated project accounting, variation tracking, and company overhead workflow. ?We have already built a working Proof of Concept (PoC). You will need to fetch incoming invoices for specific projects, map the JSON data to our database, and send approval signals back to Tripletex when the "Approve" button is pressed in Telegram . ?Production Deployment: Upgrade the current Flask development server to a robust production environment on our existing Contabo Windows Server (e.g., using Waitress/Gunicorn, Nginx/IIS). ?Security: Secure the API keys and sensitive data using environment variables (.env). Implement basic authentication (login) for the web dashboard. ?Customer Change Module (Kundeendringer): Create an interactive web form/interface on the dashboard where we can manually log customer changes. Include examples of similar API integrations, database forms, or Flask dashboards you have deployed

Booking confirmations & reminders. Send confirmations for jobs the sales team has booked and manage the reminder sequence leading up to each job so nothing falls through. General administrative support. Handle scheduling, document prep, and vendor coordination, and resolve light customer issues under $200 without needing to escalate. title: Finance & Accounting Coordinator
description: About the Role: New Beginnings Moving & Hauling is looking for a sharp, detail-driven part-time finance coordinator to keep the money side of the business clean and current — invoices out on time, receivables chased, books up to date, and a clear monthly picture for the owner. This is a focused, behind-the-scenes seat built for someone who lives in QuickBooks and catches the small errors before they become big ones. It is not a management or customer-facing role. Core Responsibilities: Same-day invoicing. Make sure an invoice goes out the same day every job is completed — no lag between work done and the customer being billed. Accounts receivable follow-up. Run a consistent past-due chase at 3, 7, and 14 days, escalating tone appropriately at each step and surfacing accounts that aren't responding. Expense tracking in QuickBooks. Enter and correctly categorize every expense so reports stay accurate and tax prep is painless. Payroll timesheet review. Check timesheets for discrepancies — missing punches, overlaps, unusual hours — and flag them. (This role reviews and flags; it does not process payroll directly.) Recurring billing & monthly summary. Bill recurring monthly contracts on schedule and prepare a simple monthly financial summary for the owner. Could Also Own (scope permitting within ~10 hrs/week): Bank & credit card reconciliation — match QuickBooks against statements monthly so the books are trustworthy. Fuel card reconciliation — match fuel card charges against the fleet log and receipts, and flag anything that doesn't line up (the company runs monthly fuel card audits — this role is a natural fit to support them). Tip payout reconciliation — verify the twice-weekly tip payouts match the jobs actually completed each work week. Accounts payable — track and schedule vendor and supplier bills so nothing goes late. Payment application & deposits — apply incoming customer payments to the right invoices and keep the deposit record clean. CPA / tax prep support — organize year-end documents, contractor 1099s, and sales-tax figures for handoff to the company's accountant. Light financial reporting — track simple health metrics like average days-to-pay (DSO) and an AR aging snapshot to include in the monthly summary. Ideal Candidate: Must have: Strong QuickBooks familiarity, genuine attention to detail, reliability with deadlines. Nice to have: Bookkeeping or small-business accounting background, comfort with spreadsheets, prior experience reconciling accounts. Not required: Management or customer-facing experience — the part-time scope is deliberately narrow.

description: Contract-to-Hire · 100% Remote (Philippines) · US Mountain Time Hours About Us & the Role We are a fast-growing roofing and exteriors company serving residential, commercial, and industrial customers across several US markets (Denver, Wyoming, Chicago, and Eastern North Carolina). We operate our own custo ---------- tal fabrication shops and bring a high degree of specialization to our work. After several years of rapid growth, we are now strengthening and unifying our systems to support our next phase. We are seeking a skilled HubSpot Administrator / RevOps Specialist to help manage and improve our CRM ecosystem. This is a specialized role, not a general data-entry position, and you will not be working on your own. You will join a dedicated RevOps team alongside our US-based administrators, with an in-house DevOps engineer handling custom code and API development, so you can focus on doing excellent work within HubSpot. Your work will be collaborative and reviewed, you will have access to senior expertise to learn from, and you will take on increasing ownership over time. We are hiring on a contract basis to begin, with a clear path to full-time for the right person. The contract period gives both sides a chance to confirm it is a strong fit. What You'll Do Administer HubSpot across Marketing, Sales, and Operations Hubs — workflows, custom properties, deal pipelines, lifecycle stages, lead scoring, lists, segmentation, and user management. Build and optimize workflows — including cleaning up and streamlining bloated or redundant automations so our systems stay fast and reliable. Build reports and dashboards that give leadership accurate, trustworthy visibility into the funnel and operations across multiple locations. Help consolidate and unify our HubSpot environment as we grow and acquire — working toward one clean, consistent experience across brands and locations. Maintain rigorous data integrity — deduplication, data quality, and reporting accuracy that holds up to scrutiny. Take over ongoing QuotaPath administration — comp-plan maintenance, troubleshooting, and day-to-day upkeep — to offload this recurring work from senior staff. (Already integrated; this is operational ownership, not a setup project.) Manage our connected toolstack — PandaDoc, CompanyCam, SalesRabbit, QuotaPath, and our marketing-technology providers — keeping native integrations healthy and data flowing cleanly. Partner with our in-house DevOps engineer on integrations and data movement. You won't build the custom middleware that transforms data between systems, but you should be able to speak knowledgeably about how that data flows and collaborate effectively on it. Scope and execute build-outs and projects with growing independence, from requirements to ship. Work within two-week sprints in ClickUp, managing your own tasks and deliverables. Partner on AI initiatives as we implement AI across our systems to speed up delivery. Document processes and create SOPs so the systems you build are durable and well-understood. Expert Collaboration. Ability to communicate, respond, and ask questions through tools such as Zoom, Loom, ---------- , and Clickup. What You Bring (Must-Haves) 3+ years hands-on HubSpot administration / RevOps experience, ideally spanning Marketing, Sales, AND Operations Hubs. Proven ability to architect properties and pipelines and build, troubleshoot, and optimize sophisticated workflows. Comfort managing HubSpot's native integrations and collaborating with technical teammates on data flows. (You won't be writing custom code or building APIs — we have a DevOps engineer for that — but you should understand how the pieces connect.) Excellent written and spoken English — you can gather requirements, explain technical concepts clearly, and communicate proactively with a US team. A process-driven, detail-obsessed approach to data and documentation. A collaborative, coachable mindset — you take direction and feedback well and raise your hand when something's unclear. Comfort working in an agile / sprint workflow and a task manager (ClickUp ideal). Ability and willingness to work US Mountain Time business hours (see Schedule below). Nice-to-Haves HubSpot certifications (Marketing Software, Sales Software, Revenue Operations, Reporting, etc.). These are free — a motivated admin usually has several. Experience consolidating or migrating multiple HubSpot portals (multi-brand, multi-location, or acquisition-driven). Experience supporting roofing, home-services, or field-sales organizations (door-to-door and virtual sales models). Hands-on experience with QuotaPath, PandaDoc, CompanyCam, or SalesRabbit. Experience using AI tools to automate or accelerate operations. Familiarity with custom-coded workflow actions (JavaScript/Python) — a bonus, not a requirement. Schedule & Engagement Engagement: Contract to start, with a clear path to full-time for the right fit. Hours: Approximately 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM US Mountain Time, eventually building to 40 hours/week. We can flex the start/end by up to about an hour. Please note: this corresponds to roughly 10:00 PM – 7:00 AM Manila time — a night-shift role. Whether you've ever consolidated, migrated, or merged multiple HubSpot portals (multi-brand, multi-location, or acquisition) — and what that involved. Whether you've administered QuotaPath or a similar commission/compensation tool, and to what depth. job_title: Personal Injury Prelitigation Client Advocate / Case Manage
description: # r – Remote Experience Required:2–3 years minimum in personal injury prelitigation case management Compensation: Based on experience About the Role We are a personal injury law firm seeking an experienced Prelitigation Client Advocate, often referred to as a case manager at personal injury firms, to manage personal injury claims from intake through settlement preparation. This is not an entry-level position. We are looking for someone who already understands the prelitigation personal injury process, including client communication, insurance claims, medical treatment tracking, records and bills, liens, property damage, case updates, and preparing cases for settlement review. The ideal candidate has prior experience working with a U.S.-based personal injury law firm and can confidently manage a prelitigation caseload with minimal training. Primary Responsibilities The Client Advocate will assist with personal injury prelitigation matters, including: Client Communication and Case Management Communicate regularly with clients regarding case status, treatment, property damage, insurance issues, and next steps. Maintain consistent client contact and document all communications. Explain the general prelitigation process to clients in a professional and client-friendly manner. Follow up with clients regarding treatment status, provider information, lost wages, photos, documents, and other case-related needs. Identify client concerns early and escalate issues to management or attorneys when needed. Insurance Claims Handling Open and monitor bodily injury, UM/UIM, MedPay, and property damage claims. Communicate with insurance adjusters regarding claim status, coverage, liability, property damage, and settlement-related issues. Request and track insurance coverage information, declarations pages, policy limits, claim numbers, and adjuster contact information. Monitor adverse insurance decisions, coverage issues, delays, and claim problems. Medical Treatment, Records, and Bills Track client medical treatment from the beginning of the case through discharge. Confirm providers, treatment dates, referrals, imaging, procedures, and ongoing care. Request, collect, review, and organize medical records and bills. Follow up with medical providers, records departments, billing offices, and third-party vendors. Identify missing records, missing bills, gaps in treatment, and incomplete provider information. Liens, Balances, and Health Insurance Identify potential medical liens, letters of protection, health insurance claims, Medicare, Medicaid, AHCCCS, ERISA, workers’ compensation, and other reimbursement issues. Track balances and lien information throughout the case. Assist with requesting updated balances, lien confirmations, and final payoff information. Maintain accurate notes regarding lien status and unresolved balance issues. Property Damage and Other Damages Assist clients with property damage issues, total loss claims, rental issues, vehicle repairs, diminished value, and related documentation. Collect wage loss documentation, photos, out-of-pocket expenses, and other damages evidence. Help ensure the file contains the information needed to evaluate damages before settlement review. Case Organization and File Management Upload, organize, label, and maintain case documents in the firm’s case management system. Keep medical records, bills, insurance documents, correspondence, photos, wage loss documents, and settlement materials organized. Maintain accurate case notes, tasks, deadlines, and follow-up reminders. Ensure files are complete and ready for attorney review when needed. Settlement Preparation Assist with preparing cases for settlement review. Confirm that treatment is complete or that the case is ready for settlement evaluation. Help gather the documents and information needed for settlement opportunities, demands, or attorney review. Prepare summaries, treatment timelines, provider lists, damages information, and other case materials as needed. Proactively identify missing items before a case is moved toward settlement. General Prelitigation Support Help move cases forward proactively from intake through settlement. Follow firm procedures and maintain high attention to detail. Communicate professionally with clients, providers, adjusters, lienholders, and internal tea ---------- mbers. Manage multiple cases while staying organized and responsive. Required Qualifications Applicants must have: 2–3 years of experience in personal injury prelitigation case management. Prior experience working for a personal injury law firm. Experience managing personal injury cases before litigation. Experience communicating with clients, insurance adjusters, medical providers, billing offices, and lienholders. Experience requesting and organizing medical records and bills. Experience tracking medical treatment and case progress. Experience handling or assisting with property damage claims. Strong written and verbal English skills. Strong attention to detail. Ability to work independently and follow instructions. Ability to organize digital files and manage multiple cases. Reliable internet connection and computer. Availability during U.S. business hours. Preferred Experience Experience with any of the following is a plus: Arizona or New Mexico personal injury claims. Case management software such as CASEpeer, SmartAdvocate, Filevine, Clio, Litify, or similar. Handling UM/UIM, MedPay, and bodily injury claims. Working with liens, health insurance reimbursement, Medicare, Medicaid, AHCCCS, ERISA, or workers’ compensation liens. Preparing cases for settlement demands or policy-limit opportunities. Reviewing medical records and bills. Spanish-speaking ability. Experience working remotely for a U.S.-based law firm. Who Should Not Apply Please do not apply if: You are new to legal work. You have no personal injury experience. You have never managed prelitigation personal injury cases. You have never communicated with insurance adjusters or medical providers. You are unfamiliar with medical records and bills. You need extensive training on basic personal injury case management tasks. You are unavailable during U.S. business hours. Ideal Candidate The ideal candidate is organized, proactive, detail-oriented, and experienced in personal injury prelitigation work. We need someone who can step into a client-facing case management role and help move cases forward without constant supervision. You should be comfortable communicating with clients, tracking treatment, organizing records and bills, following up with providers and adjusters, identifying missing information, and preparing files for settlement review. This role requires someone who cares about clients, keeps cases moving, and understands that strong prelitigation case management directly affects case outcomes. How to Apply Please submit: Your resume. A short explanation of your personal injury prelitigation experience. The types of personal injury cases you have handled. The case management software you have used. Your experience with medical records, bills, liens, insurance adjusters, and settlement preparation. Your expected monthly salary. Your availability to work U.S. business hours. In your application, please include the phrase: Experienced PI Client Advocate

Requirements & Qualifications Experience: 5+ years of dedicated experience in international VAT compliance (specifically EU VAT) and full-cycle bookkeeping. You will work closely with Viktor, Frederik, and RJ on real client accounts, with real budgets, and see the direct impact of your work. You will be at the forefront of AI-driven creative production — not reading about it in newsletters, but actually building it. If you are someone who is energized by change, loves building things, and wants to be part of a team that genuinely cares about doing great work — this is the place for you. description: All-round Digital Growth Marketer: property tech plus a new SaaS, remote The short version We are a European property-tech group and we need someone who can build our growth across the board. Not one channel, the whole picture: SEO and content, paid, social, AI search, influencers, email , and new international channels. You can do a bit of all of it, you go deep where it counts, and you love finding new ways to reach people. If you can prove what you have grown, read on. Who we are We run several live rental platforms in the European market on one shared codebase, including an established rental and property-management brand and a more modern consumer rental platform. The rental platforms are where most of our volume is today. On top of that we are launching a new in-house SaaS product in the hiring and recruitment space, which you help grow from the start. So you get both: established brands with real traffic, and a new product where you shape growth from day one. How we work Small team, fast pace, real ownership. We care about clear communication, good decisions, and results we can measure. We use AI tools to move faster and we expect you to do the same, as long as you check and refine before anything ships. We work async and in writing. Your first days 1. Get our analytics and conversion tracking in solid shape, so we can actually see what works. 2. Find the quickest wins across the channels we already have, and start improving them. 3. Run the first acquisition experiments for the new SaaS product. From there you open it up: SEO and content, paid, email and lifecycle, social, AI search visibility, influencers, and international channels. We want someone who keeps finding new ways in, not just running the obvious ones. What you will own over time - The full growth picture across the rental platforms and the new SaaS: which channels we use, what we test next, and what actually moves the numbers. - SEO and content (NL and EN): search, on-page, listings, and content that ranks and converts. - Getting us visible where people actually look now, including AI search results and answer engines, not just Google. - Paid where it earns its place (Google, Meta), plus email and lifecycle automation. - Social, brand, influencer and creative channel experiments, including international audiences. - Analytics and simple conversion improvements on listing and signup pages, with clear reporting. What we are looking for - Real digital marketing experience with results you can explain, in numbers. - Broadly skilled: comfortable across SEO, content, paid, social, email and analytics, and able to go deep where it matters. - A channel explorer: you have opened up or tested channels beyond the obvious ones and can show it. - Strong written English. Dutch is a strong advantage. If you do not write Dutch, you must be comfortable managing translation and native review. - Self-managing, reliable, and good at written async communication. - Ideally 6 hours overlap with CET business hours, Monday to Friday. Tell us your timezone and the window you can cover. Nice to have - Property, real estate, or marketplace marketing. - SaaS or early-stage product growth. - Marketing automation or CRM, landing-page and conversion work, light design. Rate and hours USD per hour depending on your experience. Part-time to full-time, ideally 20 or more hours a week to start. This is a long-term role: strong work and real results move both your scope and your rate up over time and grow with results. How we start (paid) We begin with a small paid, time-boxed task we agree upfront, to see how you analyze, prioritize and execute on something real. No unpaid speculative campaign work, ever. If it clicks, we move into the ongoing role. How to apply (English, no template letters) Start the first line of your reply with: Growth that ships. Then tell us: 1. One channel you grew, with the actual result (numbers, before and after). 2. A channel or tactic you tried that most people would not think of, and how it went. 3. How you use AI tools in your work, and how you keep quality in check. 4. The two or three channels you are strongest in, and where you are still growing. 5. A link to your portfolio or one thing you are proud of. 6. Your hourly rate in USD, hours per day you can commit, your CET overlap window, and your earliest start date. Do not apply if - You are not the person who will do the work. - You cannot show or explain real results. - You only run one channel and do not want to work across the rest. - You ship AI-generated content without checking it. Skill requirement: Digital Marketing, SEO, Content Marketing, Social Media Marketing, Analytics Employer: M. Oosterom

People apply through our website and give us their phone number — so every lead you contact has already raised their hand. This is NOT cold calling. Your job is to reach these warm leads fast, by text AND phone, build trust, answer their questions, and book them into a 15-minute call with our team. WHAT YOU'LL DO Respond FAST to inbound leads — speed is everything Run the winning sequence: send a quick intro text, then call the lead (we'll train you on this) Talk to leads on the phone: build rapport, answer common questions, calmly handle "is this legit?" Qualify leads with a few simple questions (e.g., do they have a Canadian-born parent or grandparent) Book qualified leads into a 15-minute call on our calendar Follow up by text and call with people who went quiet Keep the conversation list clean — no lead left unanswered Log notes and update lead status so nothing slips WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR Clear, confident spoken English with a neutral accent — you'll be on the phone with cautious U.S. leads, so they need to trust your voice immediately. (This is the #1 requirement and we will assess it from your video — see below.) Excellent written English — natural and friendly over text Comfortable and confident making and taking phone calls (this is a phone-forward role) Reliable and self-managing across a 7-day schedule — consistency matters more than long hours Fast and responsive — quick replies and quick dials are what book calls Experience with chat/SMS, phone, or CRM tools (SendBlue, GoHighLevel, HubSpot, dialers — a plus) Available on U.S. Eastern hours, including weekends Stable internet, a quiet place to take calls, a reliable computer, and a good headset Bonus (not required): Prior appointment-setting, sales, telemarketing, customer support, or live-chat experience Experience working with U.S.-based leads or customers COMPENSATION DETAILS Base: $4 USD/hour for scheduled hours (~20–25 hrs/week) Booked-call bonus: $5 USD for every qualified booked call "Qualified" = the lead confirms a specific date/time, has a real Canadian-born parent or grandparent, and is genuinely interested. (We pay for quality bookings, not junk.) Paid weekly or bi-weekly (your preference) Long-term role. Reliable performers get raises and more hours. HOW TO APPLY (READ CAREFULLY — incomplete applications are deleted) 1. Start your message with the word "MAPLE" at the very top, so I know you actually read this. 2. Record a short custom video (2–3 minutes) — THIS IS REQUIRED. No video = no consideration. In the video: Introduce yourself on camera, speaking in English so we can hear you clearly Tell us specifically why YOU are a good fit for THIS role — not a generic intro. Mention that it's a text + phone setting role and that you'd be calling warm leads about Canadian citizenship. Reusing an old generic VA video will be obvious; we want one made for this job. Briefly describe any experience you have calling or texting leads, setting appointments, or doing sales/support End with this: pretend a lead just said "How do I know this is even legit?" — say out loud, in your own words, exactly how you'd respond to keep them comfortable and move toward booking a quick call. Upload it to Google Drive, YouTube (unlisted), or Loom and paste the link. 3. In writing, tell me: your available hours per week, and which days/times (in U.S. Eastern time) you can work. Applications that don't start with "MAPLE" or don't include the custom video will not be reviewed. We'll run a short paid trial with real conversations before any long-term offer. title: Social Media Manager
description: What This Role Actually Is 4ocean pulls plastic out of oceans, rivers, and coastlines, and turns the story of that work into a brand that customers want to be part of. Social media is how most of the ---------- et us. This role is the daily engine behind that. You take direction from the e-commerce and marketing leads and turn it into posts that go live, on time, on brand, every day. You ideate inside the strategy we set. You build the assets. You schedule the posts. You answer the comments and DMs. You boost what is working and run the simple paid campaigns we hand you. You report the numbers back honestly. This is an executor role, not a strategist role. The brand voice, the campaign themes, and the testing priorities come from us. The shipping, the polish, and the steady daily output come from you. We are not looking for someone who waits for instructions on every post. We are looking for someone who runs a calendar inside a clear playbook and makes a hundred small, good decisions a week without needing to escalate them. What Success Looks Like: Three months in, the daily content engine runs without me chasing it. The calendar is full two weeks out. Posts go live when they are supposed to, formatted right for each platform, with captions that sound like 4ocean. Community responses do not pile up unread. Reporting shows up Monday mornings without being asked for, and it tells me something I can act on. Six months in, you are bringing me content angles and trend ideas I had not thought of, and a meaningful share of them are working. Boosted posts and the small paid campaigns you run are improving on basic metrics. You know our audience better than I do on a day-to-day level because you are living in the feeds and the comments. What You'll Do Organic Content Production • Build the short-form vertical video we post to TikTok and Instagram Reels, mostly editing from existing footage, b-roll, and creator content using CapCut, etc.. • Design static posts and carousels in Canva using the brand kit and templates we provide. • Write captions in 4ocean's voice. We will give you examples, voice guidelines, and feedback in the first weeks until it lands consistently. • Pitch three to five content ideas per week that connect to current trends, ocean and sustainability news, or product ---------- nts. We pick what ships. Calendar, Posting, and Scheduling • Maintain the weekly and monthly content calendar in Asana. Two-week rolling visibility minimum. • Schedule and publish across Instagram, TikTok, Facebook , and any new channels we add. Right format, right copy, right hashtags, right time for each platform. • Coordinate with the e-commerce and email teams so social posts line up with launches, promos, and lifecycle campaigns. Community Management • First-line responses to comments and DMs across all channels. Standard responses for FAQs, escalation to customer service or me for anything sensitive, off-script, or PR-adjacent. • Flag negative sentiment, recurring complaints, or PR risks the same day they appear. • Engage with creators, partners, and customers who tag us. Build the habit of conversation, not just broadcasting. Paid Social Execution • Boost organic posts that are earning it, using the rules we set together. • Set up and duplicate ad sets in Meta Ads Manager and TikTok Ads Manager from briefs we provide. Audiences, placements, budgets, creative uploads, naming conventions. • Swap creative on running campaigns, refresh assets on a regular cadence, pause underperformers when they hit our thresholds. • This is not media buying. You are not building strategy from scratch. You are running the playbook we hand you, cleanly and consistently. Reporting • Weekly numbers every Monday. Reach, engagement, follower growth per channel, top three and bottom three posts of the week, paid spend and basic performance against the targets we set. • Short written commentary, two or three sentences, on what stood out and what you would try next. • Monthly roll-up with trend notes for our review. Who Thrives Here Someone who: • Treats deadlines as real and a content calendar as a commitment, not a suggestion. • Has strong written English and can write a caption that sounds like a brand, not a translation. • Edits short-form vertical video fast and well in CapCut. Not perfectly cinematic. Native to the platform. • Is comfortable inside Meta Ads Manager and TikTok Ads Manager from clear instructions. • Notices things. Sees a comment trend, a competitor move, a ---------- cycle, and surfaces it without being asked. • Asks good questions early and does not let small ambiguities become missed posts. If you need someone to walk you through every step every day, this will not work. If you want to run a daily operation inside a clear system and grow into more responsibility as you prove it, this is the role. Experience That Matters • Two-plus years running social media for a brand, an agency, or a meaningful number of clients. DTC and ecommerce experience preferred. • Portfolio showing real short-form vertical edits you have shipped, not just stock template work. • Hands-on experience inside Meta Ads Manager and TikTok Ads Manager. Not certifications. Actual campaigns you have set up and managed. • Comfortable in Asana or a similar project management tool. We run our entire operation in Asana. • English fluency at a level where I do not have to rewrite your captions before they go live. Tools You"ll Use • CapCut, etc. for video, Canva for static and carousel. • Meta Business Suite, Meta Ads Manager, TikTok Ads Manager. • A social scheduler we will set you up in. Likely Later, Metricool, or similar. • Asana for the calendar and task management. • Google Drive and Slack for files and team communication. • AI tools where they help you move faster. We will share what we use. How to Apply: Send a short message telling me which brands you have run social for and what your best result was. Attach two or three short-form vertical edits you made and a screenshot of a Meta or TikTok ad campaign you set up. No long cover letters. Shortlisted applicants will be invited to a brief paid trial: one reel edit from footage we provide, three caption variations, and a one-page content calendar for a hypothetical product launch. Paid at the hourly rate. Make sure to attach your updated resume link.

Discovery is moving from celebrities to friends — the way Spotify made music social, Goodreads made reading social, and Strava made running social, we're making shopping social. We're early, we're growing fast, and we need someone to own how that growth actually happens. That's you. ???? You live in Claude Code / Codex / Cursor and you're obsessed with growth as a craft. You own customer outcomes — full stop. Installs, activation, retention, listings, virality — whatever moves the number. You build the engine, you run it, you iterate weekly until the metrics move. Then you do it again :) ? What you'll build Three engines, all AI-native: 1. AI Ad Factories Spin up high-volume, high-velocity ad creative + landing pages. Dozens a week, all instrumented, all tested. You own CAC, ROAS, and the LTV math. 2. Zero-to-One PLG & Onboarding Our onboarding is our growth. You'll build and A/B everything from first-open to first-listing to first-share — automating the path that turns a download into an obsessed user. 3. Algorithm Hacking — AI Social & Virality Engines TikTok, Reddit, IG, SEO/AEO, influencer sourcing — you build the systems that crack distribution. Agents that source creators, generate content, find the threads, ride the algorithm. This is where we win or lose, literally. Whatever moves the customer's KPI — outbound, content, Reddit growth, AEO, partnerships — you build it, run it, iterate. ???? Who you are You ship. 3–5 things a week, and you know which 2 actually matter. You're a real builder — TypeScript / React / Next.js, SQL, an experiment platform (Statsig / GrowthBook / whatever). You can stand up infra, not just templates. You live in AI tooling — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor — and you build agents, not just Zapier flows. (If your whole stack is no-code, this isn't the fit — and that's totally okay!) You're scrappy, fast, and allergic to 3-week architecture debates. Growth is a craft to you, not a job title. ???? Bonus points You're genuinely obsessed with fashion, resale, or social commerce You've done growth at a consumer app or marketplace before You have channel instincts — you feel where attention is moving Please note: you don't need to have done all of this before — but you do need to be the kind of person who figures it out fast :) ???? We're seed-stage, so expect real equity, real ownership, and a real say in the soul of the platform. If you've ever wanted to help shape an early-stage product from zero — this is your ---------- nt. title: Full-Stack Developer (TypeScript / React / Node / Supabase
description: **READ THIS ENTIRE POST BEFORE APPLYING** This post is direct on purpose. It saves your time and ours. Applications that ignore the instructions at the bottom will not be replied to. And to be upfront about the process: text answers don't get you hired here. A screen-share does. If you're not willing to show your real work, live, on camera, stop reading now. ABOUT US 1 DASH ( ---------- ) is a US payments and merchant services company with 20+ years in the industry, serving businesses nationwide. Our stance with our customers is simple: "Running a business is hard. Your payments shouldn't be." The software behind that promise is what you'd be building: a payment and invoicing SaaS, an agent dashboard, a mobile app, and internal analysis tools. Our values are simplicity and transparency, in the product and in how we work. That's also why this post is blunt. Small dev team, zero bureaucracy, and the features you ship get used by real businesses to move real money. THE STACK (THIS IS WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY WORK IN) • TypeScript everywhere, strict mode • Frontend: React 18/19, Next.js 15/16, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI, TanStack Query, React Hook Form, Zod • Backend: Node 20, Express APIs • Database: Supabase (Postgres + Auth), Drizzle ORM and Prisma • Mobile: React Native / Expo with NativeWind and Zustand (nice to have, not required) • Integrations: payment processor APIs (Valor, Dejavoo), OpenAI, Resend, webhooks • Testing: Vitest, Playwright, Supertest • Infra: Vercel, Railway, GitHub Actions, pnpm / Turbo monorepo You do not need every item on this list. You do need to be genuinely strong in TypeScript, React, Node/Express, and SQL/Postgres. WHAT YOU'LL DO • Build features end-to-end: database schema, API endpoint, UI • Fix bugs without being babysat • Write typed, Zod-validated code that passes lint, typecheck, and tests before you say "done" • Work with payment APIs and webhooks. This is fintech, correctness matters more than speed. • Use AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) daily. We expect this. We don't care that you use AI, every good dev does now. We care whether you understand what it produces, and we will verify that live. WHO THIS IS FOR • Mid to senior level: around 3-5+ years of real, shipped work • You can take a loosely defined task and come back with a working, tested feature • You communicate proactively. Blocked means you communicate the same day, not three days later. • You use AI tools heavily however, you can read, verify, and fix everything they produce. If you cannot explain your own code line-by-line on a call, please do not apply. You will be asked to. Please DO NOT APPLY IF • You're an agency or you plan to subcontract the work • You need step-by-step instructions for every task • You cannot explain code you've submitted without an AI tool open • You will not record a Loom video or join a live screen-share call PAY AND SCHEDULE • $10 per hour. This is the rate. • Part-time, around 20 hours per week to start. Can grow into more (and full-time) if you're good. • Flexible schedule, long-term role. THE HIRING PROCESS (SO YOU KNOW WHAT YOU'RE SIGNING UP FOR) 1. Application (instructions below) 2. 15-minute live screen-share call. You'll open your own code from the project in your Loom, and I'll ask you to walk through specific files, explain decisions, and reason through a change on the spot. I'll also show you a small snippet from your codebase and ask what it does and what's wrong with it. No prep needed if the work is actually yours. Note on the call: AI tools must be closed during it. Not because we're anti-AI (you'll use Claude Code daily here) but because the call tests the one thing AI can't do for you: understanding. HOW TO APPLY. FOLLOW THIS EXACTLY Read carefully, because the first instruction is not where you expect it. Somewhere in this paragraph is your first filter: the first line of your application must be the word SHIPIT followed by the name of the database from our stack list above. Applications missing either are deleted unread. If you pasted this post into an AI tool and skimmed its summary, you've probably already failed. 1. Attach your resume, or include a Google Drive link set to "anyone with the link can view". A locked link counts as no resume. 2. Record a Loom video, 3-5 minutes. This is the core of your application. Requirements: o Introduce yourself briefly on camera (face visible at the start) o Say today's date and the word from your application's first line out loud o Walk through ONE project you built. Show the actual code in your editor or the live app. No slideshows, no reading from a script. o Open the git history or git blame on at least one file and show your commits o Explain one hard problem you solved AND one design decision you'd make differently today o Videos showing tutorial projects, cloned repos, or code you can't git-blame to yourself are an instant rejection 3. Answer ALL of the questions below, numbered. Skipped questions = deleted application. Keep answers SHORT, 2-3 sentences each. We can tell the difference between concise-because-you-know and long-because-AI-padded. QUESTIONS: EXPERIENCE (links over stories, everything you claim should be checkable) 1. Years of professional experience, and the biggest thing you've shipped that is live right now. A link is required: live URL, App Store listing, or public repo. "I can't link anything" needs a one-sentence explanation (NDA, internal tool, etc.) plus the closest verifiable substitute. 2. Rate yourself 1-10 on each (be honest, the live call and test task will verify): TypeScript, React/Next.js, Node/Express, Postgres/SQL, Supabase. 3. One feature you built end-to-end, database to API to UI. Link the live feature, repo, or PR/commit range, and tell me which parts you personally wrote. 4. Have you worked with payments, fintech, or third-party API webhooks? One concrete example with specifics (which processor/API, what you handled). 5. GitHub or portfolio link. If your GitHub is empty, link whatever you HAVE built instead. QUESTIONS: AI WORKFLOW 6. Which AI coding tools do you use daily and for how long? Then in 2-3 sentences: your last real task with one, what it got wrong, and what you fixed manually. (This gets verified on the call, so be accurate, not impressive.) QUESTIONS: AVAILABILITY 7. How many hours per week are you actually available, and in what timezone? Generic copy-paste cover letters will be deleted. AI-polished applications might slip past me here, but they do not survive the screen-share, so you're only wasting your own time. Only shortlisted applicants will hear back from us. If you followed everything above, you are already ahead of 90% of applicants.

description: Job description: HR Recruiter — Remote, Build Our Hiring Funnel End-to-End - Read Ad In Full One Janitorial — Remote, Full-time, Contract. You'll report to our Operations Manager and work closely with three department managers (Sales, Service, BCO). This is a high-volume, high-skill recruiting role. Source candidates across multiple channels Run inbound funnels on Indeed, JobStreet, OnlineJobs.ph, Computrabajo, LinkedIn Jobs Do cold outreach on LinkedIn Recruiter — this is a non-negotiable skill. Follow our process exactly, then improve it We have a documented recruiting SOP. You will follow it precisely for the first 60 days You will use our AI bot daily to look up rubrics, interview guides, role requirements, and policy After 60 days, you'll have earned the right to suggest improvements — backed by data, not opinion We update our process every month based on what's working. You'll be part of that 4. Own the candidate experience Every applicant gets a response within 5 business days — no exceptions Rejected candidates get a polite, branded "no thanks" with the door left open Top candidates get fast, clear communication through every stage We measure candidate NPS. You're responsible for it. 5. Report weekly to the Operations Manager Funnel volume by source Conversion rates at every stage Cost-per-hire by role Time-to-fill by role Pipeline gaps and what you're doing about them Who You AreBackground (non-negotiable) 5+ years of recruiting experience, at least 2 of which were at high volume (40+ hires/year) You've worked at a remote-first company for at least 2 years You've recruited for roles in BPO, customer service, sales, or operations — this matters because our roles look like those You speak and write fluent, professional English. You can describe how You're comfortable with high volume — 400+ applications/week doesn't scare you You've done reference checks regularly and know what questions to ask Personality (non-negotiable) You follow process before improving it. If you read this and thought "but I'd do it my own way," you're not the right fit. We have a system. You learn the system first Detail-obsessed — you don't miss steps, you don't skip rubrics, you don't make gut calls Direct communicator — you can tell a hiring manager "this candidate isn't a fit" and back it up Low drama — when challenged, you respond with data, not feelings High pace — we move fast and expect you to keep up Curious about systems and tools — you read manuals when handed them What This Job Is Not So you can self-select honestly: This is not an HR generalist role. No payroll, no policy work, no benefits administration. Pure recruiting This is not a coordinator role. You're not scheduling interviews and processing paperwork. You're sourcing, screening, and selecting This is not a "do it your way" role. We have a documented system. You follow it. After 60 days, you earn the right to improve it This is not a low-volume role. If you've only ever filled 10–15 roles per year, this will overwhelm you This is not a slow company. We move fast, we measure everything, and we expect the same of you If after reading this you're thinking "this is the role I've been looking for," please apply. If you're thinking "I could probably do most of this," please don't. Compensation & Logistics Salary: See top of post. Based on experience and market Location: Fully remote. description: Thank you for applying. I'm an entrepreneur based near Houston, Texas, and I'm hiring one sharp, trustworthy Executive & Personal Assistant to become my right hand across both my personal life and a portfolio of businesses — including MVK Construction (general contracting and custom builds), Next Space Realty (a real estate brokerage), and a couple of growing consumer ventures. Comfort with software/tech is a plus. US real estate or construction experience is a bonus, not required. --- HOW TO APPLY --- Before we move to a Zoom interview, please send a reply that includes: 1. Your answers to the screening questions below 2. Your answers to the written interview questions below IMPORTANT: So I know you read this whole posting carefully, please start your reply with the word "BLUEPRINT" in all caps. Your time zone, and which hours you can reliably work in US Central Time (Houston) 3. Are you available full-time (40 hrs/week)? If not, how many hours? 4. Earliest start date / current notice period 5. Years of EA / VA experience 6. Have you supported a U.S.-based business owner before? Briefly, doing what? 7. Have you done personal/lifestyle assistant work (calendar, travel, appointments, errands, family scheduling)? (Yes/No + 1 sentence) 8. Are you comfortable supporting two people (me and my wife) and handling personal/family + financial matters with full discretion? (Yes/No + 1 sentence) 9. Bookkeeping: What's your level — data entry, full-charge bookkeeping, reconciliations, financial reports? Which tools and for what kind of businesses? 10. Software testing / tech: Have you tested apps or websites and reported bugs, or used tools like Trello/Notion/Jira? (Yes/No + 1 sentence) 11. Any real estate or construction admin experience? (Yes/No + 1 sentence) 12. Your monthly or hourly rate expectation (state PHP or USD) Tools — rate yourself 1–5 (1=none, 5=expert): 13. QuickBooks Online ___ 14. Bookkeeping / reconciliations ___ 15. Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets) ___ 16. Microsoft Excel ___ 17. A CRM (any) ___ — which one(s)? ________ 18. E-signature tools (DocuSign / similar) ___ 19. General tech comfort / software testing ___ Reliability: 20. Your home internet speed (Mbps) — run a quick speed test 21. Do you have backup internet and backup power? (Yes/No) 22. Do you work from home, an office, or a co-working space? --- WRITTEN INTERVIEW QUESTIONS --- Please answer each with a short, honest paragraph: A. Why this role? What appeals to you about being one person's right hand across personal life, several businesses, and the books — and why are you a fit? B. Prioritization: It's a busy morning. A client is texting about a late material delivery, an inspector needs a document in the next hour, and I've asked you to finish an invoice batch. I'm unreachable for 20 minutes. What do you do, in what order, and why? C. Two principals: My wife asks you to rearrange her week because a family commitment moved, while I've asked you to keep my Thursday afternoon clear for a closing. The two schedules now collide on Thursday. How do you handle it? D. Bookkeeping: Walk me through how you'd keep the books clean across several businesses — invoicing, categorizing expenses, monthly reconciliation. What's your process for catching errors? E. Software testing: Have you ever tested an app or website and found problems? How do you approach finding what's broken and writing it up so the developer can fix it fast? F. Ownership: Tell me about a time you caught a mistake or a dropped ball — financial or otherwise — before your boss noticed. What did you do? G. Discretion: You'll see personal messages, family details, client contracts, and financial accounts. How do you think about handling sensitive personal and financial information? H. First two weeks: If I hired you today, what would you do in your first two weeks to make my life — personal, business, and financial — easier, without me spelling everything out? Take your time and be honest — this person will be close to my personal life, my family, and my finances, so trust matters as much as skill. If your answers are a strong fit, I'll invite you to a 30-minute Zoom call. Looking forward to reading your reply. Best, Vin (Vinesh Kumar) — Greater Houston / Tomball, TX

title: Virtual Assistant, Operations & Admin Support
description: Virtual Assistant, Operations & Admin Support Athena Nutrition LLC | Remote Athena Nutrition is a women focused online nutrition and fitness coaching company. I help busy women, mostly moms and women in their 30s to 50s, build sustainable habits without restriction, shame, or quick fix nonsense. The business is founder led by Katy, a coach with a healthcare background and a personal story of sobriety that sits at the heart of the brand. I am growing, and right now there are more good ideas and moving pieces than there are hours in the day. I need a sharp, detail obsessed right hand to own the operations and admin so the coaching and the client experience never slip through the cracks. This is an admin and operations role. It is not a coaching role and not a sales role. You will work alongside our creative VA (who handles design and content creation) and Katy, the coach and founder (who handles all coaching and sales conversations). Your job is to make everything around those two run like clockwork. Who you are: - Get it done attitude. You move things across the finish line without being chased. When something is incomplete, you own the follow-up. - Detail oriented to a fault. You catch the missing signature, the failed payment, the client who never connected their app. Nothing slips. - Self-disciplined and proactive. You spot what needs doing and do it, rather than waiting to be told. - Resourceful. When you hit an obstacle, you find a way around, through, over, or under it before you bring it to anyone. - Tech-savvy. You enjoy figuring out new tools. If software frustrates you, this is not your role. - Warm and discreet. You will handle sensitive client information, including health details and personal struggles. You treat it with total confidentiality and care. - Comfortable with our world. Our brand touches on health, body image, and recovery from drinking. You do not have to share that story, but you do need to be at ease around it. - An eye for clean and organized. You like things tidy, findable, and done well. Who you are not: - Someone satisfied with "good enough." - Someone who needs a safe, predictable, identical routine every week. This is a solo founder business with a lot of motion. What is predictable is that things change. - Someone who drops balls and lets them stay dropped. What you will own: - Own onboarding follow through. If a new client has not booked their kickoff call or connected MyFitnessPal, you are the one nudging them, so the coach never has to think about it. - Handle offboarding and renewals admin: process pauses and cancellations, set up renewal payments after the coach has the re-sign conversation, and request testimonials and before and after photos on the way out. - Flag who has not checked in or is missing data, and send the reminder nudges. - Prep a simple one page "last month" summary before each monthly 1:1 so the coach walks in informed. - Maintain the master client tracker and move it into Airtable: status, start date, renewal date, goals, milestones. Surface birthdays, client anniversaries, and weigh-in wins so the coach can send a personal note. - Run group call logistics: reminders, posting the recording to the Drive library, updating attendance. - Keep the GoHighLevel pipeline clean and correctly tagged by stage (hot, warm, cold). Building this structure out is part of the role. - Each morning, hand the coach a "who needs a follow-up today" list pulled from the pipeline, so the day starts with zero hunting. - Calendar, inbox, and scheduling - Monitor Stripe for failed and declined payments, and chase them down. - Keep a running sheet of MRR, churn, and new revenue. - Keep the Google Drive resource library organized and tagged so guides and videos are easy to find. - Maintain and update SOPs. Several already exist and need someone to keep them current as things change. - Handle basic GoHighLevel and Clockify upkeep and light automation troubleshooting. - Triage comments and routine DMs: sort them, answer the simple and repetitive ones, and escalate anything that looks like a real sales lead straight to the coach. You do not sell or handle objections. - Keep the Facebook group warm: welcome new members, post prompts, and keep an eye on it. Tools you may use: Trainerize, GoHighLevel, Stripe, MyFitnessPal, Canva, Google Workspace and Drive, Clockify, and the usual social platforms (Instagram, Facebook , TikTok). Experience with any of these is a plus. Willingness to learn all of them is required. Logistics, hours, and pay: - 100% remote. Roughly 5-8 hours per week to start, with some weeks lighter and some heavier around launches or deadlines. Real room to grow into more hours and more responsibility as you prove yourself. - Because some tasks are time sensitive, I need a few hours of weekly overlap with US Eastern business hours, preferably 8am-11am EST. The rest of your schedule is flexible. - Starting pay: $8 per hour, with clear room to grow based on performance.  I am protective of downtime, yours and mine. Plan your time off, keep the balls in the air, and long weekends and vacation are no problem. How to apply: Send a short note telling me why this role fits you, plus any relevant experience with the tools above or in a coaching, nutrition, fitness, or environment. So I know you read this all the way through: start your message with the word "Athena" and tell me, in one sentence, which part of this role you would be best at and why. I review applications as they come in and will reach out to set up a quick conversation. I am excited to find the person who helps me reach more women!
